Stable-3.1.0.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.1.0

Denne udgivelse er resultatet af en fuld audit af alle tester-rapporter (~40 sager fra
Freedom, EnvyNYC, cpuff1989, Knuckleduster, Merlyn95, Solski, infiL, Maegis, Manne,
dirtyjob13) plus en gennemgang af hele koden. Rapporterne viste sig at koge ned til nogle
få systemiske rodårsager — dem er der rettet i, i stedet for at lappe symptomerne.

Kræver **Multiworld Launcher London 2.8.4**.

---

## Ting der ødelagde dine karakterer

**Skill points forsvandt ved Hell (og "negative skillpoints")**
Modden samler karakterens samlede skill-point-total i et .d2s-felt der kun kan rumme 255.
Ved 256+ point rullede tallet rundt (280 blev til 24), og næste login nulstillede stort set
alle dine skills. En Paladin krydser statistisk 256 præcis omkring NM-afslutningen — derfor
så det ud som om Hell-overgangen var skyld i det. Nu clampes feltet, og overskuddet gemmes i
moddens egen fil og gives tilbage ved næste load. Samme behandling for stat points (1023-grænsen),
og skill-pointen kan ikke længere tælles ned under nul.

**Reinvest tvang dig til respec**
Hvis genindsættelsen af dine skills ikke nåede at køre inden for 30 sekunder, blev ALLE dine
investerede point smidt tilbage i puljen — en tvungen respec, typisk hvis du var AFK på en
load-skærm. Timeouten er væk: modden prøver nu igen, også hen over sessioner, og venter ikke
længere på at du trykker på en tast.

**Stack-overrun ved hver character-load**
En ubunden indlæsning kunne skrive ~190 bytes uden for sin buffer hver gang du loadede.
Samtidig blev en intern bitmap skåret over, hvilket fik guld-milepæle og set-pickups til at
fyre igen hver session, og fik chest-kvoten til at vokse indtil chest-checks blev umulige at nå.
Begge dele er rettet.

**Items forsvandt i stash**
- Luk stash med ESC mens du har et item på musen → itemet blev slettet. Nu udskydes lukningen.
- Shift-click mod en fuld stash → itemet blev fjernet fra kilden uden nogensinde at blive lagt.
  Nu rulles hele flytningen tilbage ("Not enough room — item returned").
- Shift-click ud af Horadric-kuben smed stash-items på gulvet. Kuben skelnes nu fra stashen.
- Runewords og andre store items blev slettet hvis de ikke kunne serialiseres. Nu beholdes de.
- Alle stash- og statistik-filer skrives nu atomisk med backup — et crash midt i en gemning
  kan ikke længere koste dig en hel fane.

---

## Checks og items der ikke kom frem

**Quests der ikke registrerede (Horadric Staff, Summoner, Khalim's Will, Hellforge,
Terror's End, Cain, Anya)**
Modden kiggede det forkerte sted efter quest-status, så en række quests først blev opdaget
når du loggede ud og ind igen. Den læser nu også spillerens egen per-difficulty quest-record.
Sikkerhedsforanstaltning: den nye kilde bruges kun hvis den beviseligt stemmer overens med
den gamle, så den aldrig kan finde på at "fuldføre" noget du ikke har lavet.

**NM/Hell-checks der ikke fyrede første gang pr. session**
Quest-linjerne blev læst op mod den forkerte difficulty. Rettet.

**Checks der blev sendt, men aldrig kom frem**
Et check blev markeret som "sendt" før det rent faktisk lå i køen — var køen fuld, forsvandt
det sporløst. Nu markeres det først når det er accepteret, og der kører en genafsendelse hvert
8. sekund.

**Ny karakter på samme slot fik ingen items**
Dedup-filen var kun navngivet efter karakternavnet, så en genbrugt karakter på en ny seed
arvede den gamle seeds "allerede leveret"-liste. Filerne er nu stemplet med seed.

**Store mængder items på én gang**
Hele backloggen blev anvendt i ét enkelt frame, og XP kunne ryge i gulvet hvis den ramte en
load-skærm. Nu højst 8 ad gangen, og resten venter i kø.

---

## Guld og XP

**XP-belønning på 415.000 blev til 37 millioner**
XP-belønninger blev givet på én tråd mens XP-multiplikatoren målte på en anden, så
multiplikatoren nåede at gange belønningen. Al flad XP går nu gennem samme kø og tælles
korrekt fra. Multiplikatoren nulstiller desuden korrekt ved karakterskift.

**Alle belønninger ramte loft ved ca. 415.000**
Tilfældighedsgeneratoren kunne kun nå 32.767. En "400k-1M"-belønning gav derfor altid ca.
415k. Rettet — hele intervallet bruges nu.

**Båret guld forsvandt ved relog**
Guld-belønninger respekterede ikke D2's grænse for båret guld (level × 10.000), og spillet
skar overskuddet væk ved næste login. Overskuddet lægges nu i guldbanken i stedet.

---

## Verden og monstre

**Tomme Tower Cellars, Crypt, Mausoleum og Durance L2**
Modden pustede antallet af rum op til Hell-størrelse i alle sværhedsgrader uden at skrue
tilsvarende op for monstertætheden — det samme monsterbudget blev spredt over mange gange
flere rum, og de tidlige niveauer endte tomme. Oppustningen er fjernet. 3.0.0's midlertidige
"auto-fuldfør Tower Cellar L1/L2" er fjernet igen, da områderne nu befolkes normalt.

**Ét tilfældigt område pr. seed var fuldstændig tomt**
Monster-shufflen kunne uddele Mountain Tops pulje (de tre Ancients, som ikke kan spawne
normalt) til et almindeligt område, der så ikke kunne spawne noget som helst. Boss-arenaerne
er nu holdt uden for shufflen.

**"Unkillable" monstre i Normal**
Monstre blev byttet på tværs af hele spillet, så en Akt 5-type kunne lande i Akt 1 med sine
fulde stats. Byttet sker nu inden for samme akt.

**Alt for høj monstertæthed udendørs**
Bundgrænsen for tæthed var sat ~2× for højt. Sænket.

**Områder der stadig var tomme efter monster-kopiering**
Når et tomt område fik kopieret en monsterpulje, fulgte antals-kolonnerne ikke med — området
havde en monsterliste, men trak nul typer. Rettet.

**Vendors solgte forkerte klassers items**
Butiks-shufflen flyttede rundt på klassespecifikt udstyr (Akara solgte Sorceress-orbs).
Klasselåst gear bliver nu, hvor det hører hjemme.

**Unsummon talte som kills**
At afkalde sine egne skeletter/ulve talte med i "Clear"-checks — flere af jer brugte det som
workaround i tomme områder. Egne summons tæller ikke længere (og med spawn-rettelserne ovenfor
burde workarounden heller ikke være nødvendig).

**Entrance-shuffle kunne gøre en seed umulig**
Halls of the Dead, Maggot Lair og Claw Viper Temple kunne shuffles om bag Tal Rasha-gravene —
som kræver Paladset, som kræver Tainted Sun, som kræver Claw Viper Temple. Et ægte deadlock
(én tester måtte bruge save-editor). De tre quest-dungeons er nu fredet og ligger altid ved
deres normale indgange; alt andet shuffles stadig.

---

## Ubers, bosser og statistik

- Pandemonium-opskriften åd dine nøgler/organer selv når intet spawnede. Nu afvises opskriften,
  og du beholder dine ting.
- Uber-trackeren blev aldrig ryddet for dræbte mini-ubers, så finale-trioen efter 5-6 runder
  ikke kunne udløse din torch. Rettet.
- Treasure Cow kunne give gratis boss-loot fra en forældet reference. Nu verificeres enheden.
- Assassin-kicks blev talt som spillerdødsfald i dine livstidsstatistikker. Rettet.
- En gate-boss der ikke kunne spawne blev alligevel markeret som færdig, hvorved zone-nøglen
  forsvandt resten af sessionen. Nu markeres den kun ved faktisk succes, med genforsøg.
- Statistikker gemmes nu løbende (hvert minut) i stedet for kun ved log-ud, så et crash ikke
  koster hele sessionen.
- Dræbte monstre kunne tælles to gange i tætte områder, hvilket fik område-quests og cow-milepæle
  til at fyre for tidligt. Rettet.

---

## Zonenøgler er lavet om (Archipelago)

Hver akt har nu **én** zonenøgle, som du får flere kopier af: den første kopi åbner
aktens første port, den næste åbner den næste, og så videre. Før havde hver port sin
egen unikke nøgle, hvilket gjorde hele spillet til én lang kæde hvor rækkefølgen var
låst — og det var grunden til at dine tidlige D2-nøgler kunne ligge gemt langt inde i
andre spillere ekstremt sent i deres spil. Nu hjælper **enhver** kopi dig videre.

Den allerførste nøgle (Akt 1, Normal) placeres desuden tidligt, så du ikke sidder fast
i startområdet.

**Bemærk:** dette kræver nye seeds. Igangværende spil kan ikke fortsætte på 3.1.0.

## Zone-låsen smider dig ikke længere ud af omdirigerede indgange

Med både zone-låsning og entrance-shuffle slået til kunne du blive smidt ud af et
område som shufflen selv havde sendt dig ind i. Det sker ikke længere.

## Regenerér kort (mod "sort væg")

Nogle spillere har oplevet en usynlig mur der blokerer vejen, og som hverken relog
eller nyt spil kunne fjerne — kortet er nemlig bundet til din gemte karakter. Der er nu
en funktion der ruller et helt nyt kort til karakteren, uden at røre level, items eller
quests. Der tages automatisk en sikkerhedskopi af din save først.

## Mindre ting

- "+X to Amazon Skills" viste "(Lionheart Only)" i stedet for "(Amazon Only)".
- Nogle check-navne var taget fra spillets interne arbejdsnavne og passede ikke til
  områderne: "Halls of Death" hed i virkeligheden Halls of Pain, "Glacial Caves"
  var The Ancients' Way og Icy Cellar, "Tundra Wastelands" var Frozen Tundra, og to
  waypoint-checks pegede på forkerte områder. Alle rettet.
- Spirit-runewordet gav Liv i stedet for Mana.
- Necromancers Summoning-tab manglede sin tekst.
- Meshif viste Cains Akt 3-dialog.
- Quest-loggen står nu på den sværhedsgrad du rent faktisk spiller, og level-milepælene har fået
  en overskrift, så det er tydeligt at de tæller med i dine checks.
- Belønninger der ankom lige før du gemte og afsluttede, overlever nu genstart.
- Når et lovet set/unique-item ikke kunne rulles, får du nu besked om hvad der faktisk kom
  (i stedet for stiltiende at få noget andet).
- Zone-håndhævelsen droppede sit forsøg på at flytte dig efter ét forsøg, hvilket gav
  "du bliver smidt ud"-beskeder mens du stod i byen. Nu prøves der igen.
- Kloakkerne i Akt 2 kunne efterlade dig strandet væk fra din portal.

---

## Kendte ting der IKKE er rettet i denne udgivelse

- **⚠ Summon IKKE Iron Golem.** En Iron Golem der bliver gemt med karakteren kan gøre saven
  uindlæselig ("unable to enter game, bad hireable"). Indtil det er løst: lad være med at
  bruge skillen. Rammer man den alligevel, ligger der tidsstemplede .bak-filer ved siden af
  din save.
- Navngivne set/unique-items kan stadig komme som et andet item af samme type (Mara's →
  Metalgrid). Motoren vælger selv; en rigtig løsning kræver dybere indgreb.
- Merc-professioner i Akt 2/3, champion-navne og diverse "an evil force"-tekster på items kan
  stadig stå blanke/forkerte. Teksterne findes i spillets strengfil, men manglende
  opslagsnøgler kan ikke tilføjes uden at genopbygge hele filen — det kræver den originale
  1.13c-udgave som reference.
- Aura-runewords (D2R-importerne) giver ikke deres aura — mekanikken findes ikke i 1.10f-motoren.
- Ubers/Pandemonium er stadig eksperimentelt og kan crashe — vi anbefaler at lade
  "Collection — Specials" være slået fra i seriøse runs.
- Summons/mercs kan fryse efter en teleport-indhentning (rammer alle followers). Genkald/
  gensummon løser det.
- Gate-bosser kan stadig kræve et par genindlæsninger før de dukker op (f.eks. Fire Eye).
- **Act 4-hunts på "ubrugte" monstre** (Winged Death, The Tormentor, Taintbreeder,
  Riftwraith) kan kun fuldføres med zone-låsning slået TIL. Spiller du uden zone-låsning,
  så lad "Hunt"-checks være fra — eller få dem frigivet af din host.
- **Entrance-shuffle er stadig ikke i logikken.** De tre quest-dungeons i Akt 2 er nu
  fredet, men Flayer Dungeon kan fortsat lande uden for Akt 3, og et par indgange kan
  pege underligt. Kombinationen zone-låsning + entrance-shuffle anbefales stadig ikke i
  multiworld.
- Radament kan efter monster-shuffle optræde som en anden enhed, så hans quest ikke
  registrerer. Undgå SuperUnique-shuffle hvis du vil være sikker.
- Enkelte spillere har mistet waypoints (kun Akt 1 tilbage). At tale med en NPC henter
  dem tilbage.
- Pit/Sewers-indgange kan stadig sætte dig af det forkerte sted i multi-etage-dungeons,
  og "The Smith" kan crashe spillet efter shuffle.
- Kort-relaterede rester: en enkelt ekstra dør i Catacombs 4, og vægge er ikke
  gennemsigtige i -3dfx-tilstand.

Stable-3.1.1.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.1.1 (hotfix)

**Opdatér med det samme hvis du er på 3.1.0.**

## Spillet kunne ikke starte på 3.1.0

3.1.0 kunne ikke starte og gav denne fejl:

```
Assertion Failure
Location : D2Lang\StrTable\strtable.cpp, line #208
Expression : usCRC == pHeader->usCRC
```

**Årsag:** 3.1.0 indeholdt en lille rettelse af spillets tekstfil (`patchstring.tbl`) —
"+X to Amazon Skills" viste forkert "(Lionheart Only)". Den fil har en kontrolsum i sit
hoved, som Diablo II tjekker ved opstart. Rettelsen ændrede teksten uden at genberegne
kontrolsummen, så spillet afviste filen og stoppede med det samme.

**Rettelse:** tekstfilen er rullet tilbage til den originale, gyldige udgave. Alt andet
fra 3.1.0 er uændret — hele resten af udgivelsen virker som beskrevet.

Konsekvens: de to tekstfejl fra 3.1.0's noter er **ikke** rettet endnu ("(Lionheart Only)"
og Necromancerens Summoning-fane). De kræver en korrekt genopbygning af hele tekstfilen
inklusive kontrolsum, og det kommer i en senere udgivelse. Det er kosmetik — ingen
gameplay-effekt.

Vi har samtidig lagt en spærre ind i vores egen udgivelses-kontrol, så en ændret tekstfil
aldrig kan slippe ud igen uden at kontrolsummen passer.

## Hvis du sidder fast på 3.1.0

Launcheren burde selv hente 3.1.1. Virker det ikke, så brug **[Verify]/reparér** i
launcheren — den henter spilfilerne igen. I værste fald: slet spilmappen og installér
forfra fra launcheren (dine saves ligger i `Save/` og røres ikke).

## Hvad var nyt i 3.1.0

Se `patch_notes_Stable-3.1.0.md` — den store fejlrettelses-udgivelse (skill points der
forsvandt, items der blev slettet i stash, checks der ikke registrerede, tomme områder,
XP- og guld-fejl, nye zonenøgler m.m.). Alt det er med her.

**Husk fra 3.1.0:** zonenøglerne er lavet om, så **igangværende seeds kan ikke fortsætte** —
der skal genereres nye. Er du midt i et løb, så bliv på din nuværende installation til det
er færdigt.

Stable-3.2.0.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.2.0

Den største opdatering siden 3.1.0. Alt hvad der er blevet bygget og testet på
experimental-kanalen de seneste uger, er nu samlet i den normale version — de to
udgaver er fra i dag identiske.

Kræver **Multiworld Launcher London 2.9.0** (opdaterer sig selv).

---

## Alle de manglende og forkerte tekster er rettet

Vi fandt årsagen til hele familien af tekstfejl: moddens tekstfil stammede fra
patch **1.09**, ikke 1.10. Den manglede over hundrede tekster, og mange numre pegede
på den forkerte. Filen er udskiftet med den ægte 1.10-udgave. Det retter på én gang:

- Lejesvendenes type vises igen i Akt 2 (Combat / Defensive / Offensive)
- Champion-monstre har navne igen (Ghostly, Fanatic, Possessed, Berserker)
- **"an evil force" er væk** — modstander-resistens, "when you Level-Up",
  "when you Die" og aura-runewords viser rigtige tekster
- Skjolde viser "Chance to Block:", sværhedsgraderne hedder Nightmare og Hell igen,
  runerne hedder Shael, Io og Jah, Necromancerens Summoning-fane har sin tekst,
  synergi- og per-level-linjer på skills er tilbage

## Iron Golem ødelægger ikke længere din karakter

Den værste fejl vi har haft: en Iron Golem kunne gøre karakteren **permanent
ulæselig** ("unable to enter game, bad hireable"). Tre lag beskyttelse:

- Golemmen gemmes ikke længere i filen (den virker normalt, men overlever ikke
  save & quit — prisen for at filen aldrig kan ødelægges)
- Allerede ødelagte karakterer kan indlæses igen
- Launcherens **Unbug Save**-knap kan reparere gemmefiler — med automatisk
  sikkerhedskopi

Og til alle der har undgået Valkyrie af frygt for det samme: vi har efterprøvet
spillets save-kode — **kun** Iron Golem gemmes nogensinde i filen. Valkyrie,
skeletter og alle andre summons kan umuligt ødelægge noget. Brug dem frit.

## Du får det item AP lovede dig

"Mara's Kaleidoscope" i beskeden men Metalgrid i tasken? Spillet valgte selv
tilfældigt blandt items med samme basis-type. Vi fandt spillets indbyggede måde at
bede om et *bestemt* item — nu er det rigtige item valgt allerede når det skabes.
Samtidig rettet: samme unique to gange virker nu begge gange, Rainbow Facets kan
skelnes fra hinanden, og du får altid besked hvis spillet måtte nedgradere et item.

## Gate-bosser og Hunt-mål er ikke længere samme monster

26 af de 44 zone-nøgle-bosser var samme monster som et "Hunt:"-mål — ét drab kunne
udløse begge belønninger. Gate-bosserne har nu **deres egne identiteter** i spillets
data: gate-bossen giver nøglen, Hunt-målet giver checket, og de kan aldrig blokere
hinanden.

## Dine summons og lejesvende fryser ikke længere efter en teleport

De blev flyttet fint med — men deres AI blev afbrudt undervejs og kun genstartet
hvis de stod helt stille i teleport-øjeblikket. Modden vækker dem nu selv, og de
"vågner" ikke længere først når de bliver ramt.

## Monster-fældernes nedbrud er rettet

De genopstående monstre (Monster Revive Trap) kunne crashe spillet. Årsagen var
ikke grafik, som vi længe troede — fælden huskede dødsstedet på en måde der kunne
blive ugyldig sekunder senere. Nu tager fælden altid udgangspunkt i din aktuelle
position; kan dødsstedet ikke nås, rejser de dræbte sig omkring dig i stedet.

## Entrance-shuffle kan ikke længere låse en seed

Khalims tre organ-dungeons (Spider Cavern, Flayer Dungeon, Akt 3's kloakker) kunne
lande bag en Akt 5-indgang — en umulig cirkel. De bliver nu på deres pladser, som
Akt 2's stav-dungeons blev fredet tidligere. Det kendte "Flayer Dungeon uden for
Akt 3"-problem er dermed løst.

## Ubers spawner forskudt

Pandemonium-trioen kom i verden på samme øjeblik — tre af spillets tungeste monstre
på én gang, hovedmistænkt i uber-crashene. Nu kommer de én ad gangen med kort
mellemrum (fejler den første, nægtes opskriften stadig, så dine keys/organer ædes
ikke). Uber Baals tentakel-angreb er fjernet (endnu en crash-kilde); hans klon-evne
og alt andet er urørt. Crasher det stadig, logges nedbruddet nu automatisk med
præcis adresse i `d2arch_crash.txt` — send den til os.

## Mindre rettelser

- Skills fra items (f.eks. Necromancer-stavens +1 Raise Skeleton) viser det rigtige
  ikon i højreklik-menuen
- Nyt testværktøj i Ctrl+V-menuen: spawn gate-bosserne én ad gangen

## Kendte spørgsmål

- **"Mine waypoints er væk i den nye akt!"** — De er ikke væk: tal med NPC'en ved
  indgangen til akten. Sådan virkede spillet i 2003; nyere udgaver gjorde det
  automatisk, så det er let at glemme.
- Aura-runewords er under afprøvning — vores research viser at mekanikken faktisk
  findes i spillet.

**Husk:** zonenøglerne blev lavet om i 3.1.x, så seeds fra før 3.1.0 kan ikke
fortsætte.

# Stable 3.2.1 — the empty-zone bug, found and fixed

Two fixes from Discord reports. Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.2** or newer
(unchanged from 3.2.0).

## 1. Zones with almost no monsters

**What you saw.** Some zones spawned so few enemies that a "Kill N monsters"
check could not be completed — Catacombs Level 2, the Tower Cellars, the Crypt,
the Mausoleum. Often the only things present were champion packs, uniques with
their minions, and gargoyle traps. Other zones of the same type were fine:
Catacombs 4 always worked.

**Why.** The randomizer's monster shuffle copies one monster's record over
another's to change how it looks, sounds and behaves, then restores the
original's stats so the difficulty stays put. Six bytes were never restored:
how rare a monster is, how many spawn per group, and how big the escort party
around a leader is.

Those six bytes are what the level generator reads to decide whether it may
place a monster **at all**, and how many. A rarity of zero means "never spawn
naturally". Across the twenty shuffle presets there are 13,520 swaps, and:

- **415** turned a normal monster unplaceable — one preset gives Fallen their
  record from Baal's High Priest, a monster the generator never places
- **2,128** collapsed a pack monster's group size to one
- **2,004** collapsed the party that spawns around a leader

A zone draws from a short list — Catacombs 2 uses three monster types. Draw two
bad ones and the zone has almost nothing left to place, and what little does
place gets upgraded to champion or unique. That is the reported symptom
exactly.

It also explains two things that never made sense before. Catacombs 4 was
always fine because it is a **preset** level: its monsters come from the fixed
map, not from the density pass. And editing the game's text files never helped
because **there was never anything wrong with them** — `levels.txt`,
`LvlMaze.txt` and `monstats.txt` in this build are byte-for-byte identical to
vanilla 1.10f. The damage was done in memory, after the files were read.

**The fix.** Those six bytes are now restored along with the stats. The shuffle
still changes everything it was meant to change; it no longer changes how many
monsters a zone gets.

This affects **Archipelago mode**. Standalone uses a different shuffle that
works on the level lists instead, and was never affected.

Existing characters benefit immediately — monster placement is decided when you
enter a zone, so a zone you have not visited yet in an existing game will
populate correctly from now on.

## 2. Kill-quest progress in the book

**What you saw.** The quest book did not seem to track "Kill N monsters"
quests.

**Why.** Kill tallies were kept in a single set of counters shared by all three
difficulties, and that set was wiped whenever the difficulty changed. Going to
Nightmare erased every Normal tally; coming back to Normal, the progress was
gone. The book also lets you switch which difficulty you are viewing, but the
numbers it showed always came from the difficulty you were actually playing —
so they were real numbers next to the wrong completion marks.

**The fix.** Kill counts are now kept per difficulty, saved per difficulty, and
the book reads the tally belonging to the difficulty you are looking at.
Existing saves are read as before and their counts land on Normal.

Kill quests live on the book's second quest tab, alongside area and waypoint
checks.
Stable-3.2.1.title: Stable 3.2.1

Stable-3.2.2.description:
# Stable 3.2.2 — the other half of the empty-zone bug

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.3**. Everything from 3.2.1 is included.

3.2.1 was supposed to fix the empty dungeons. It fixed one of the two faults
behind them, which is why Tower Cellar and the Catacombs were still coming up
barren afterwards. This is the other one.

## Tower Cellar and the Catacombs

The monster shuffle copies a monster's whole record and then puts back "the
fields that matter". 3.2.1 restored the six bytes that decide whether the level
generator may place a monster at all. What it did not restore is `MonStats2` —
which was treated as cosmetic, because it holds the sprite and the animation.

It also holds the monster's **collision footprint**.

Across the 40 shipped shuffle presets, **48.5% of all swaps changed that
footprint**. The Tower Cellar's own monster gets inflated from 2×2 to 3×3 in 52
of them, and once to 0×0, which cannot be placed anywhere at all.

That is why the reports split the way they did:

| | |
|---|---|
| Tower Cellar 1-4, Catacombs 1-3 | generated mazes — **barren** |
| Tower Cellar 5, Catacombs 4 | fixed layouts — fine |

A fixed-layout level puts its monsters on marked spots, where the size does not
matter. A maze has to fit them into rooms it generated, and a 3×3 body fails
the fit test again and again where the 2×2 the level was designed around would
have passed. What survives is the champion packs, the uniques, and the traps
that are part of the map — exactly what people described. With only three
monster types per level, two bad rolls is enough to empty it.

Swaps that would change a monster's footprint are now refused outright, the
same way the ban list refuses quest bosses. Just over half of all swaps still
apply, so the variety is still there, but the placement geometry is now
identical to vanilla and cannot drift again.

If a zone still comes up empty, the log line now reads three numbers — applied,
skipped by ban list, skipped by size guard — which says immediately whether the
shuffle is involved at all.

**No seed regeneration needed.** This changes what happens at runtime, not what
the seed contains.

## While we were in there

Every one of the game's 136 areas was checked against the original data. Six
are empty, and all six are meant to be: the tower and harem entrances, Shenk's
siege, the Ancients' summit, the temple entrance, and Baal's chamber. Nothing
is missing monsters by accident. The area data files themselves turned out to
be byte-for-byte identical to the original in every copy we ship, so past
attempts to fix this by editing them were never going to work.

## Treasure cows

A treasure cow was a level 28 monster no matter where it turned up, and it got
a **flat** health bonus on top — around eight times its own health in Act 1.
Diablo II derives a monster's health regeneration from its maximum health, so
that multiplied the regeneration by the same amount. That is the cow that would
not die.

It now scales to your character's level and takes its bonus health as a
**percentage** of its own, so the regeneration stays in proportion. It is still
a boss-tier fight, roughly two and a half times a normal monster of your level,
with resistances lowered to match. It should feel worth killing rather than
impossible or pointless.

## Skill editor

Two new buttons under the skill list:

**Hide Locked** collapses the list to only the skills you can actually use.

**Colourblind** stops the list depending on colour. Rather than adding another
palette — red/green and grey/green were both ruled out by testers, and a third
set of colours is still just colours — each square gets its tier as a number,
and locked squares get a dash. That works for every kind of colour blindness,
not only the common one.

Both settings are remembered between sessions.

Two things fixed in the same pass: the skill list was still capped at 260
entries from before the pool grew, and an unlocked skill with an unexpected
tier was drawing on the red "locked" square and reading as locked when it was
not.

Stable-3.2.3.description:
# Stable 3.2.3 — one file to send when something goes wrong

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.4**. Everything from 3.2.2 is included.

## If you crash, send one file

The game has been writing a detailed crash log for a long time, but nobody knew
it was there. Crash reports arrived as the launcher's clipboard diagnostics
instead, which contains no crash information at all — so every report needed a
follow-up conversation just to find the file that already existed.

That is fixed from both ends.

**The launcher now saves a complete report by itself.** When a game crashes, a
single zip appears on your Desktop — `Multiworld-Rapport_<date>.zip`. It holds
the crash log, the run log, your settings and the launcher's own state, for
every game you have installed. Send that one file and nothing else is needed.
There is also a **Save Problem Report** button in Settings if you want one
without crashing.

**The game now writes a real crash dump.** Alongside the existing log there is
now a `.dmp` file with an actual call stack, which is the difference between
knowing where a crash happened and knowing how it got there. The crash log also
marks the fatal exception clearly, so it stands out from the harmless
first-chance noise around it.

Nothing personal is collected — only logs and configuration from the game and
launcher folders.

## A crash on cube transmutes

Transmuting in the Horadric Cube could hard-crash the game. It was
intermittent, which is why it did not reproduce when people tried.

The on-screen notification text was being built directly into the buffer the
game draws from, one character at a time, while the drawing code was reading
that same buffer. If the drawing happened to look in between the first
character landing and the end-marker landing, it read past the end of the
buffer and the game died.

The cube transmute was unusually exposed to this because its check fires from
the game's own logic, while nearly every other notification comes from the same
side that draws. The treasure cow's warning had the same problem. Notifications
are now finished before they are handed over, so a half-written message can
never be drawn.

This also fixes a smaller bug: a notification longer than the buffer used to
write nothing at all, leaving the previous message on screen.

**Whether this was the crash people hit is not yet confirmed** — it is a real
fault on exactly that path, but no crash dump existed to prove it. That is
precisely what the report above now captures, so if it happens again we will
know for certain instead of reasoning about it.

## Testing

If you crash, look on your Desktop. The zip should be there already.
Stable-3.2.3.title: Stable 3.2.3

Stable-3.2.4.description:
# Stable 3.2.4 — instrumentation for the empty-zone reports

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.4** (unchanged). Everything from 3.2.3 is
included.

Zones are still coming up empty for some players, and this round proved the
previous two fixes were real bugs but not this bug: the latest reproduction had
the monster shuffle and zone lock switched **off**, and every data file —
including the engine's own compiled tables — checked out byte-correct.

That leaves the engine's monster-placement code, where four different steps
could be failing and reading the code cannot tell them apart. So this release
measures instead of guessing.

## What it does

Every time you enter a level, one line is written to the game's log:

```
CENSUS: area=36 diff=0 | rec den=680 num=3 nrm=3 ... | live rooms=41 act=7 mon=0 obj=12
```

The first half is the level's spawn configuration exactly as the running engine
sees it; the second half is a count of what actually stands in the level's
rooms at that moment. Between them, one visit to an empty zone pins down which
step is failing — data loading, monster placement, or client sync — instead of
another round of theory.

There is no gameplay change in this release. If you hit an empty zone, just
play on — the log line is already written, and the problem report zip from
3.2.3 picks it up automatically.
Stable-3.2.4.title: Stable 3.2.4

Stable-3.2.5.description:
# Stable 3.2.5 — tier colours for real, and a sharper census

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.4** (unchanged). Everything from 3.2.4 is
included.

## The skill list finally shows its tiers

The pool squares were meant to be green for tier 1, blue for tier 2 and orange
for tier 3 — but every unlocked skill drew green. The whole chain was suspected
and cleared one piece at a time: the tier data was right, the files loaded, the
drawing code picked correctly. The cause was the art itself: the blue and
orange squares were generated from the green template and literally contained
green pixels, with the intended tier colour only as a two-pixel line hidden
under the skill icon.

The squares are regenerated with the full border in the tier colour. Locked
stays red.

**The tier number in the corner is now always shown.** It arrived as a
colourblind aid, but reading a digit beats decoding a border colour for
everyone, so it is permanent.

**Colourblind mode now changes the colours themselves:** tier 1 becomes white
and locked becomes dark grey, while blue and orange stay — that palette
contains none of the pairs colourblind players confuse, and the digits carry
the rest.

## Census, round two

The first census run answered two of three questions: the spawn configuration
survives loading intact, and monster units do exist near a level's entrance.
What it could not tell is *which* monsters — and the reports specifically say
the leftovers are champion packs and gargoyle traps, which count as monsters
too.

The census now lists what it found by monster class, and re-counts every eight
seconds while you stay in a level, so walking deeper shows whether rooms keep
receiving monsters as they activate. One walk through a barren zone and the
log tells the whole story.
Stable-3.2.5.title: Stable 3.2.5

Stable-3.2.6.description:
# Stable 3.2.6 — the census closes in

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.4** (unchanged). Everything from 3.2.5 is
included. No gameplay change — this narrows the empty-zone hunt further.

The 3.2.5 census established that a barren zone is not actually empty: the
champion packs, superuniques with their retinues, and the shooting traps are
all there. What never appears is the regular trash population — and the spawn
configuration itself is intact.

That points at the two engine services the trash-spawn code depends on and the
boss placement does not. This release asks them directly: on every level entry
the log now records how many rooms the engine considers populatable and what
the room's spawn-area list actually contains. Whichever of the two comes back
broken is the bug; if both come back healthy, the fault is pinned inside one
specific function and the next step is surgical.

Walk into any barren zone once and the log has the answer.

# Stable 3.2.7 — the empty zones are fixed

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.5**. Everything from 3.2.6 is included.

Zones that spawned only champion packs, superuniques with their retinues and
gargoyle traps now populate normally.

## What it was

The mod shipped a rebuilt copy of one of Diablo II's engine libraries in its
`patch` folder. That folder is not a set of optional extras: the loader takes
every file in it and rewires the game's own functions into it, one at a time.
Shipping that rebuild therefore replaced the whole of that library's exported
surface — around thirteen hundred functions.

Two of them are what the ordinary monster-spawn path calls, and they are not
used by the code that places champions and bosses. That is the exact asymmetry
every report described, and it is why a "barren" zone was never actually empty.

Measured on the same seed and character, Catacombs Level 3:

| | monsters found |
|---|---|
| before | 10, nearly all rats and bats |
| after | 66, including 16 zombies and 18 dark ones |

The file is no longer shipped. Because updates unpack over an existing install
and never remove files that stopped being shipped, the game also deletes any
leftover copy before every launch — so this fixes itself whether you update
through the launcher or run the game directly.

## Why it took several attempts

Two real bugs were found and fixed along the way — the monster shuffle
destroying the fields that decide whether a monster may be placed (3.2.1), and
the same shuffle changing monsters' collision size so they no longer fit the
rooms (3.2.2). Both were genuine, both are still fixed, and neither was this.

What found it in the end was measurement rather than reasoning: the census
added in 3.2.4 proved the spawn configuration was intact, 3.2.5 showed exactly
which creatures were present, and an A/B test with the file removed settled it.
Those census lines stay in the build, so a future report of this kind can be
answered from one log instead of four rounds.

## Also

Skill tier colours now actually differ — the blue and orange squares were
generated from the green template and contained green pixels. The tier number
in the corner is permanent, and colourblind mode switches tier 1 to white and
locked to grey.

# Stable 3.2.8 — F1-F4 belong to your skills again

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.5** (unchanged). Everything from 3.2.7 is
included.

## The mod's panels have moved to 5, 6, 7 and 8

F1 to F4 are Diablo II's first four skill hotkeys, and the mod had taken them
for its own panels. That is why the right-click skill selector would only let
you bind F5 and upwards: the key never reached the game, because the mod
consumed it first.

The panels now sit on the number row, where 1-4 are your belt and 5 upwards
were unused:

| | |
|---|---|
| **5** | Skill book |
| **6** | Quest log |
| **7** | Tracker |
| **8** | Zone map |

Assigning a skill to F1-F4 works again with nothing else to do. If you had
already customised these keys they are left alone; only a binding still sitting
on F1-F4 is moved, and your ini is updated so it sticks.

## The mouse wheel now cycles your skills

This one was never broken — Diablo II 1.10f simply has no mouse-wheel binding
at all; it arrived in later versions of the game. So it is implemented here.

With no mod panel open, rolling the wheel steps through your skill hotkeys,
down for the next and up for the previous. Inside the skill book, quest log,
tracker or zone map the wheel still scrolls that panel, exactly as before.

It walks eight slots by default. A slot with nothing bound is stepped over
rather than skipped, so if you use fewer, set `WheelSkillSlots` under
`[keybindings]` in `Archipelago\d2arch.ini` to the number you actually use and
the wheel will only walk those.

# Stable 3.2.9 — tooltips that say what a skill IS

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.5** (unchanged). Everything from 3.2.8 is
included.

## Tooltips

A tooltip used to give you a name, a flavour line and a damage number. That is
not enough to tell an aura from a trap from a curse — and several skills
reported as "does nothing" turn out to have no direct damage by design.

Every skill tooltip now opens with **what kind of skill it is** — Aura, Trap,
Summon, Curse, Passive, Melee or Spell — followed by a mechanics line: the
element, the damage and how it grows per level, the mana cost, and whatever is
specific to that kind (how many pets at once, an aura's radius, a trap's shot
count).

Where a skill genuinely has no direct damage, it now says so instead of leaving
you to guess. An aura that is missing its effect data says that too, in the
tooltip, rather than silently doing nothing.

The classification is read from the skill's own mechanics, never from its name
— which matters, because a few skills called "Aura of …" carry no aura data at
all, and that mismatch is now visible instead of hidden.

## Skill logging

The game log now records every time you switch to one of the new skills, with
its id, tier and name. If you are working through skills one at a time and
writing notes, the log lines line up with your notes afterwards.

The problem report from 3.2.3 picks the log up automatically — the zip on your
Desktop already contains it.

# Stable 3.3.1 — the skill pool slider means what it says

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.6**. Everything from 3.3.0 is included.

Setting the skill pool slider to 30 — or 1 — still produced every vanilla
skill. Maegis called it, and there were two separate faults behind it:

**The game never applied the value.** The pool was always built with every
skill; the number only filtered what one list displayed in Archipelago mode.
The slider now governs membership: at 30, exactly 30 vanilla skills exist in
that seed's pool, chosen at random per seed and spread proportionally across
the tiers (30 becomes 10/10/10; 1 becomes a single tier-1 skill). The rest
never appear — not as unlocks, not as rewards, not in the book.

**The launcher overrode the slider.** With the experimental pack enabled it
silently wrote the maximum instead of the chosen value. It now writes what you
set; the pack sits on top of that count, all-or-nothing, as designed.

Two deliberate exceptions to the cut: your own class's class-locked skills
always survive (the randomizer never places them and losing them would break
the class), and in Archipelago mode the pool is governed by the world
generator exactly as before — the option in your YAML decides, and the game
does not second-guess it.

The retired duplicates from earlier rounds are excluded before the count, so
they no longer occupy slider slots either.

# Stable 3.3.2 — kicking a pot is not dying

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.6**. Everything from 3.3.1 is included.

**DeathLink no longer fires when you kick a breakable.** The death detector
read the player's animation mode and treated mode 12 as "dead" — but 12 is
KICK. Every kicked pot, urn or basket (and every assassin kick skill)
broadcast a death to the whole multiworld while the kicker stood there
perfectly healthy, which is exactly the prank Ormrdorr discovered. The
detector now uses the two real death modes (dying animation and corpse), so a
DeathLink goes out only when your character actually dies.

**An incoming DeathLink now does something to you.** On current launchers
another player's death only printed a notification. It now also springs the
DeathLink trap — a monster pack on your position, the same response the old
bridge always used. A guaranteed instant kill needs a verified engine damage
call and careful hardcore testing, so that stays on the research list; until
then the trap is the strongest safe response.

# Stable 3.3.4 — the key list is actually on screen now

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.6**. Everything from 3.3.3 is included.

**The panel was drawn 242 pixels too high.** Diablo II places a sprite by its
BOTTOM edge, not its top — the mod's own in-game panels already compensate for
that, but the new main-menu panel did not, so all you saw was the bottom border
line jammed against the top of the screen. It now sits where it belongs, in the

**F1 to F12, not F1 to F4.** The panel said F1-F4 for your skill hotkeys. All

# Stable 3.3.5 — the gate-key logic hole, found and closed

Requires **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.6**. Everything from 3.3.4 is included.

**A third of zone-locking seeds could not be finished.** Measured, not
estimated: 12 seeds generated with the 3.3.4 apworld, 4 of them placed an Act 2
key inside Tal Rasha's Tomb 4 or 5 — rooms that need all four Act 2 keys to
enter. The last key sat behind its own gate, Duriel could never be reached, and
Act 3 never opened. The same shape was reachable in Act 1 (Catacombs Level 4),
Act 3 (Ruined Fane) and Act 5 (Crystalized Cavern).

The cause: 33 checks had no zone recorded, so the logic treated them as
reachable from the very first minute regardless of which gates were shut. Every
one now carries the zone the game itself uses, taken from the mod's own quest
table, and a guard refuses to generate at all if a check ever loses its zone
again. Re-measured after the fix: 30 seeds, 540 key placements, zero dead.

**Nihlathak's Temple is no longer treated as free.** The three Halls and the
Temple are never gate-locked — but they are only reachable through the red
portal Anya opens, and Anya is one gate deep in Act 5. A key could therefore be
hidden behind a portal that only exists once that key had been used. They now
require the Act 5 region-2 key, which is what the game actually demands.

**Entrance shuffle combined with zone locking is now safe.** The shuffle deals
dungeons across acts on purpose, so a cave the logic believes is in Act 1 can
physically end up behind Act 2's last gate. With both settings on, checks in
any shuffle-movable dungeon are now junk-only — nothing you need can be hidden
somewhere the logic cannot see. Verified over 15 seeds: no key landed in a
movable zone.

**Killing an act boss finally does something.** The act-completion item the
logic uses had no handler at all, so beating Andariel, Duriel, Mephisto, Diablo
or Baal produced complete silence — no message, no log line. It now announces
the act is open, and repeats for every act instead of only the first.

**Two settings that used to break quietly**

- Skill Class Filter on with every class switched off now refuses to generate
  instead of producing a character with no skills at all.
- Using `exclude_locations` in your YAML no longer risks "not enough filler
  items": the skill pool now leaves room for them up front.

Also fixed: the Monastery Gate check demanded one gate more than the game does.

**New verification tooling** (`Tools/`): `ap_logic_sweep.py` drives
Archipelago's real generator over every option — each one isolated, all the
gate/entrance/goal combinations, 400 random configurations, and mixed
multiworlds with eight other games — and `ap_model_vs_dll.py` cross-checks the
logic model against the mod's own zone tables, which is what caught this.
`ap_gate_placement_audit.py` is the before/after measurement quoted above.
Stable-3.3.5.title: Stable 3.3.5

Stable-3.3.6.description:
# Stable 3.3.6 — check a seed before you play it

Includes **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.7**, which this release ships.

## New: "Check a seed…" in the launcher

On the Diablo II page, next to Graphics settings. Give it the spoiler file from
a generated multiworld (and your YAML if you like) and it answers one question:
**can this seed actually be finished?**

It does not take Archipelago's word for it. Archipelago proves a seed is
beatable under the logic it was given; this rebuilds the world the game will
really build — including running the exact same entrance-shuffle permutation
the mod will run — and then walks it: collect what you can reach, use the keys
you found to open gates, repeat. Anything still out of reach at the end is
reported by name, with the reason.

The verdict is APPROVED or NOT APPROVED. A failure reads like this:

> "Clear Tal Rasha's Tomb 5" needs 4 Act 2 key(s) to enter, and the key that
> opens the way is inside it.

It also reports, without spoiling anything:

- **Spheres** — how many there are and how many checks open up in each, so you
  can see whether the seed front-loads or drip-feeds.
- **Where the entrances went** — "Den of Evil is now entered from Hole (Act 1,
  region 3)". Zone locking and entrance shuffle together effectively redraw the
  map, and this is the part no one could see before.

## Required for that: Archipelago worlds are now reproducible

The mod's master seed — which drives the entrance shuffle, the monster shuffle
and every reward pre-roll — used to come from the system clock in Archipelago
games. The same multiworld therefore produced a different map on every
character, and nothing outside the game could know the layout, which is exactly
why a seed check was impossible until now.

It now uses the stable per-slot key the launcher already derives from the
multiworld's seed and your slot name. Same multiworld and slot means the same
world, every time. Characters created before this update keep the layout they
already have.

Everything from 3.3.5 is included.
Stable-3.3.6.title: Stable 3.3.6

Stable-3.3.7.description:
# Stable 3.3.7 — the seed check is where you play, and the map follows your seed

Includes **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.8**, which this release ships.

**"✔ Check seed" now sits in the Play row**, next to Unbug Save — where you
already are before you start — instead of buried in the settings page. Same
check as 3.3.6: hand it a spoiler and it tells you whether the seed can be
finished, names anything that cannot be reached, and reports the sphere layout
and every moved entrance without revealing a single item.

**The Map tab now lists areas in the order your seed actually opens up.** It
used to be sorted the way the vanilla game runs, which is the wrong order the
moment zone locking or entrance shuffle is on — the list showed a sequence
nobody plays. Areas are now grouped by the gate that stands in front of them,
and each row carries a small **R1–R5** tag: R1 is open from the start of the
act, R3 means it sits behind that act's second gate. Hover it for the plain
wording.

With entrance shuffle on, that ordering follows the shuffle: a dungeon is
placed where its *new* entrance is, not where the vanilla map put it. The
launcher works this out by running the same permutation the game runs, reading
the seed the same way the game does — from the ini in a solo run, from the
Archipelago slot data in a multiworld. Nothing to configure; open the Map tab
and it matches what you are playing.

Everything from 3.3.6 is included.

# Stable 3.3.8 — the seed check now reads real multiworld spoilers

Includes **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.9**, which this release ships. The game side
is unchanged from 3.3.7.

**2.9.8's check could not read a spoiler with more than one player.** It
assumed the wrong line format, found no Diablo II placements, and said so
instead of judging the seed. Single-player spoilers were unaffected. Maegis and
Solski asked exactly the right question about multiworld — this is the answer.

**Items in other players' worlds are now handled properly.** A gate key of
yours placed in someone else's game is recognised and counted as obtainable:
whether that player can reach it is Archipelago's own logic, which it already
proved when it generated the seed. The report tells you how many of your items
sit in other worlds and how many of those are gate keys, so the verdict is not
mistaken for a guarantee about the whole multiworld.

What the check uniquely adds is unchanged, and is the thing Archipelago cannot
see: a gate key hidden behind the very gate it opens, in your own world.

Verified against three spoilers — a one-player seed, a three-player multiworld
with two Diablo II slots, and a seed known to be dead, which is still correctly
rejected.

# Stable 3.4.0 — seed check no longer rejects gate-less seeds

Includes **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.11**, which this release ships. The game side
is unchanged from 3.3.9.

**A seed with Zone Locking switched off was reported as impossible.** The check
applied the gate model to every seed, including ones where there are no gates
at all and nothing can sit behind a key. It was caught building a two-slot test
multiworld: the slot with gates passed, the slot without them failed. If the
checker told you a perfectly ordinary Skill Hunting seed was broken, that was
this — and it was wrong.

A gate key lying in your world but addressed to another player is also no
longer counted as yours. It opens nothing for you, and crediting it could have
hidden a real dead end.

Stable-3.4.1.description:
# Stable 3.4.1 — Alt latches, a hidden-stats page, and the seed check stops guessing

Includes **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.12**, which this release ships.

## Alt now latches

Holding Alt to see what is on the floor is fine for a second and tiring for a
whole session. Tap Alt once and the item labels stay up; tap again and they go
away. The game is never told anything new — it still just sees Alt held, which
is exactly what a controller's left trigger has always done here. What changed
is who decides when to let go.

The latch drops by itself when you alt-tab away, open one of the mod's panels,
or open the cheat menu, so the key can never end up stuck in another program.
Set `ShowItemsToggle=0` under `[keybindings]` in `Archipelago\d2arch.ini` for
the old hold-to-see behaviour.

Also fixed while in there: a remapped "ShowItems" key never worked, because Alt
arrives from Windows as a system key and the remapper only looked at ordinary
ones.

## New book page: Hidden Stats

Press **5**, then the **Stats** tab. The character screen shows a curated
handful of numbers; this page shows the ones that actually decide a run:

- **Magic Find** and **Gold Find**
- **Resistances as raw → now / cap**, so you can see your Hell headroom rather
  than only what counts in the area you are standing in
- Elemental damage you add — fire, lightning, cold, poison — and Enhanced Damage
- Attack Rating, bonus to hit, Crushing Blow, Deadly Strike, Open Wounds, Pierce
- Faster Cast, Hit Recovery, Block and Run/Walk
- Physical and magical damage reduction, +All Skills

Totals include worn gear **and charms carried in the inventory** — the game
applies those to the character itself, so nothing is estimated.

## The seed check stops guessing

It derived the entrance-shuffle seed from the spoiler and got a different
number than the game does. Measured against a real play log: the reproduced
permutation matched **31 of 31** entrances with the game's seed and **1 of 31**
with the derived one. The maths was right and the input was wrong, which is the
worst kind of wrong — the answer looked detailed and confident.

It now reads the seed the game itself uses, from `Archipelago\d2arch.ini`. When
that is unavailable it reports "APPROVED for the normal map — entrance layout
not checked" instead of inventing a layout.

## Map tab order

Within a gate band, areas now follow the order you actually meet them instead
of the alphabet: the town sits at the top of its act, and Blood Moor comes
before Cold Plains.
Stable-3.4.1.title: Stable 3.4.1

Stable-3.4.2.description:
# Stable 3.4.2 — reconnecting no longer re-delivers everything

Includes **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.14**, which this release ships. **Update
both.** Either half alone fixes most of it; together they close it properly.

## The bug

Every reconnect handed players stat points, skill points and items they had
already received.

Archipelago replays your entire item history on every connect — that is by
design, and the mod is what remembers which of them already landed. It keeps
that record per character and throws it away when it decides you are in a
different world.

It kept deciding exactly that. The key naming the world could be either the
launcher's number or, when the launcher had not written one yet, your slot name.
Both are correct names for the same world, but the mod compared them as plain
text: number, slot name, number, slot name — every flip read as a new seed and
took the delivery record with it.

Two changes, one on each side of the pipe:

- **The launcher always writes the key now.** It never needed the slot data it
  was waiting for; the room seed and your slot name are enough. Same value every
  launch, and the same value used for the data tables and the save folder.
- **The mod only compares like with like.** A key is stamped with where it came
  from, and a record is only discarded when two keys from the *same* source
  genuinely differ. A record with no stamp — every character before this
  release — is adopted rather than thrown away, so the update itself does not
  cost you one. A genuinely new seed still clears the record, and a slot change
  still clears it exactly, by its own (server, slot) fingerprint.

Anything wrongly re-delivered before this is already in your character; the mod
now stops adding more.

## Also fixed: switching character swallowed fillers

The per-location record that stops filler items from arriving twice was not
cleared when you switched character in the same session. The next character
started with the previous one's locations already marked, so its stat points,
skill points and gold were silently dropped. It cleared the other half of the
record correctly, which is why this only ever hit fillers.
Stable-3.4.2.title: Stable 3.4.2

Stable-3.4.3.description:
# Stable 3.4.3 — the mod now tells you which version it is

Includes **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.15**. Game logic is unchanged from 3.4.2;
this is about being able to diagnose the next problem.

## It has been lying about its version since 3.3.2

The version shown in-game, written at the top of `d2arch_log.txt`, printed by
the mod loader and sent over the launcher pipe all said **Stable 3.3.1**, no
matter which build you were running.

The version lived in two places: three numbers, and a hand-written copy beside
them. Everything user-visible was derived from the numbers — except the crash
report, which used the copy. The copy was kept up to date. The numbers were not.
So the crash report was right and everything else was two weeks stale.

It came to a head asking a tester which version he was on: his log answered
3.3.1 while he was running 3.4.2. That is a bad way to start a bug hunt.

The copy is gone; everything derives from the three numbers now. And the
eleven-character limit on the in-game version slot — the reason 3.3.9 rolled to
3.4.0 rather than 3.3.10 — is checked by the compiler instead of remembered, so
a too-long version fails the build rather than corrupting the text next to it.

## Cleaner bug reports

"Collect logs" listed every game the launcher knows about, installed or not. A
real report arrived at 26 KB, of which 24 KB was games the player does not own.
It now lists what is installed and counts the rest.
Stable-3.4.3.title: Stable 3.4.3

Stable-3.4.4.description:
# Stable 3.4.4 — the other half of the reconnect bug

Ships **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.15** unchanged from 3.4.3.

3.4.2 fixed one reason the mod re-delivered items you already had. A player's
log after updating showed it was still happening, and pointed straight at the
second reason.

**Some items arrive without a location.** Most come tagged with the check they
were found at, and that tag is what the mod uses to know a filler — gold, stat
points, skill points, a rolled item — has already been handed over. It has to
work that way: several copies of the same filler from *different* checks all
have to land.

A handful arrive with no tag at all. Those slipped past both defences: there was
nothing to key the per-location record on, and the by-id record was deliberately
skipped for fillers. So they were applied again on every single connect, for the
life of the seed.

In the log that found this, **21 items** had no tag — four lots of stat points
and two skill points among them — and every one of them came back each time the
player rejoined.

An untagged item is one the server granted directly rather than one you found,
which happens once, so the mod now records those by id. Two genuinely distinct
untagged copies of the same filler would collapse into one; that is a far better
failure than an endless stream of them, and the log says so when it happens.
Stable-3.4.4.title: Stable 3.4.4

Stable-3.4.5.description:
# Stable 3.4.5 — Alt works again, and the latch is done properly

Ships **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.16**.

## What 3.4.1 got wrong

The Alt latch did not work, and it took ordinary hold-to-see down with it. Both
halves of that attempt were built on a wrong assumption.

**D2 does not read the window message for Alt.** It asks Windows for the key
state — `GetKeyState(VK_MENU)` — each time it decides whether to label the items
on the ground. Verified in the binary: D2Client has exactly one such call site.
So swallowing the message, which is what 3.4.1 did, changed nothing.

**And an injected key-down cannot outlive your finger.** The synthetic Alt was
overwritten a fraction of a second later by the real release. Worse, the
injected key-*up* on every second tap landed while the key was genuinely held,
cancelling the highlight mid-press. Net effect: the key did nothing at all.

## What it does now

The mod redirects the key-state call D2Client actually makes, and answers "Alt
is held" while the latch is on. Nothing is injected into Windows, no other
program can see it, and the physical key behaves exactly as it does unmodded —
because the message is now passed straight through instead of being eaten.

Tap Alt once, the item labels stay up. Tap again, they go. The latch also drops
when you alt-tab away, open one of the mod's panels, or open the cheat menu.
Because there is no synthetic key any more, it cannot get stuck in another
application — there is nothing to get stuck.

If the mod cannot install that redirect for any reason it says so in the log and
switches the latch off, leaving plain hold-to-see rather than something
half-working. `ShowItemsToggle=0` under `[keybindings]` in
`Archipelago\d2arch.ini` turns the latch off by choice.
Stable-3.4.5.title: Stable 3.4.5

Stable-3.4.6.description:
# Stable 3.4.6 — the book's new page fits inside the book

Ships **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.16**.

## The Stats tab was sitting on top of Sets I

Every tab may have its position pinned in `d2arch.ini`, and an install that
predates the Stats tab has pinned positions for the eleven tabs it knew about
and nothing for the twelfth. So eleven tabs kept their old places and the
newcomer took a slot computed for a row of twelve — landing on Sets I, half a
row too high.

The row now carries a layout version. When the file was written for an older
row it is ignored and the whole row is laid out together, so a tab can never
again be placed against a layout the others are not using. The row also shares
its width out by label length instead of in equal slices, so "Overview" gets
room and "AP" does not take more than it needs. Anything you pin by hand still
wins.

## The page ran off the bottom

The right column held four sections and overshot the page by about forty
pixels: "Misc" and "+ All Skills" were drawn onto the background art below it.
The footnote was worse — it ran straight through the Back and Next buttons.

Speed has moved to the left column, which had the room. Both columns now end
above the buttons, and the footnote sits under the right column where nothing
else is. Nothing was cut: every number that was there is still there.
Stable-3.4.6.title: Stable 3.4.6

Stable-3.4.7.description:
# Stable 3.4.7 — the actual reconnect bug

Ships **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.16**. **This is the one.** 3.4.2 and 3.4.4 each
closed a real hole, but neither was the main leak. This is.

## Gold, stat points, skill points and experience were never recorded

Every filler you receive is supposed to be remembered by the check it came from,
so the server's replay on the next connect can be recognised and ignored. The
record exists and works — but the two lines that write and read it were sitting
inside the branch that handles charms, set pieces and uniques.

Everything else went through a different branch and was never recorded at all.
Gold, stat points, skill points, reset points, experience: nothing written,
nothing to match against, so every single one arrived again on every connect.
Log out and back in and you get them again. Do it ten times and you get them ten
times.

The report that found it made this unmissable: a level-1 character holding
**75 unspent stat points and 35 million experience**, gaining another 35 points
and a million experience between two logins. And in the log, every suppression
named 45519, 45520 or 45521 — the three item drops. Not one other filler was
ever suppressed, because not one other filler was ever recorded.

There is one rule now, at the one place every filler passes through: a filler
that carries a location is remembered by its location, and one that carries none
is remembered by its id. The same reward from a *different* check still pays,
which is the whole reason the record is keyed on the check rather than the item.

## What this means for your character

Anything already granted stays — the mod stops adding more, it does not take
back. The first connect after updating still delivers what your character has
genuinely not received yet; from the second connect on, a reconnect should be
silent. If it is not, send the log.

Experience is banked rather than applied instantly: the levels land on your next
kill, which is why a character can sit at level 1 holding millions of it.
Stable-3.4.7.title: Stable 3.4.7

Stable-3.4.8.description:
# Stable 3.4.8 — several characters in one seed

Ships **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.17**. Update both.

## A second character used to get nothing

Items belong to the slot, not the character, so every character you play in a
seed is entitled to everything the slot has received. That is what makes another
character worth having while you wait on the rest of a multiworld: a different
build with the skills you have been given, and gear and gold passed between them
through the shared chest.

The mod keeps its record of what has already been applied **per character** —
that part was right, and is what stops anyone receiving the same thing twice.
What was wrong is that the launcher walks the server's item stream forward as it
delivers and only rewound it at launch. Make a second character at the
character-select screen and it sat at the end of that stream: no gold, no stat
points, no skills, nothing at all, until the game was closed and reopened.

The mod now tells the launcher which character is playing. On a name it has not
seen, the stream rewinds and the server resends, and the new character's own
record filters out whatever it already had. Nothing arrives twice, nothing is
missed, and you no longer have to leave the game to do it.

## What is per character, and what is shared

Per character — each one keeps its own, and none of it leaks across:
what it has already been given, which of your checks it has completed, its quest
flags, its stat and skill point ledgers, and its banked experience.

Shared across the seed — deliberately: the chest, so you can move items and gold
between your characters, and the checks themselves, because a check belongs to
the slot and is only ever sent once.
Stable-3.4.8.title: Stable 3.4.8

Stable-3.4.9.description:
# Stable 3.4.9 — the Stats tab says "Stats"

Ships **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.17**, unchanged from 3.4.8.

Two things you could see on the new page, both cosmetic, both mine.

**The tab wore the Zones button.** Each tab's word is painted into its own DC6 —
nothing is drawn over the top. There is no `tab_stats.DC6` yet, and asking the
game's loader for a file that is not there gets you back the last one it did
load. That was Zones, so the row showed "Zones" twice and the second one opened
Stats.

The mod now checks the file exists before asking for it, and writes the tab's
name on it as text when there is no art. The offsets for doing that have been in
the tab bar since it was built and had never been used, because until now every
tab had art. Drop a `tab_stats.DC6` into `data\global\ui\SPELLS\` whenever and
the art takes over — text is only the fallback.

**The page title ran across Runes and Gems.** "Hidden Stats" was drawn at the
same height as the tab row. It is gone: the tab you are standing on already says
where you are, and both columns carry their own headings.
Stable-3.4.9.title: Stable 3.4.9

Stable-3.5.0.description:
# Stable 3.5.0 — the book leaked six pages every time you logged in

Ships **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.17**. Includes everything from 3.4.9.

## The crash on logging in and out

Going through the character-select screen makes the book reload its artwork.
Six pages, about 70 KB each, read fresh from disk every time — and the handles
to the previous six were never given back. They were only forgotten, which is
not the same thing. Log in and out enough times and the game runs out and dies.

The tab strip a dozen lines above has always released its cels before reloading;
these six were simply missed. Every other place in the mod that reloads artwork
was checked at the same time — fourteen of them, and the other thirteen were
already doing it correctly.

Care was needed on the release order: a missing left or right page falls back to
the legacy one, so two of those pointers can be the same allocation. The
duplicates are cleared before anything is freed, so nothing is handed back twice.

## What this does not explain

The mod's crash log recorded no unhandled exception for this and there was no
minidump, so this is the strongest lead rather than a proven cause. What it
definitely is: a real leak, on the exact action that triggers the crash, in code
that draws every frame the book is open. If logging in and out still kills the
game after this, the report will now be a clean one to chase.

The access-violation entries that do appear in that log — the ones at teardown,
reading a game pointer that has already been freed — are caught by design and
have been there since 3.2.0. They are noise, not this.

(The version rolls to 3.5.0 rather than 3.4.10 because the in-game version slot
holds eleven characters and "Stable3.4.10" is twelve. Since 3.4.3 that limit is
checked by the compiler, so the build refused to produce a wrong string rather
than quietly corrupting the text beside it.)
Stable-3.5.0.title: Stable 3.5.0

Stable-3.5.1.description:
# Stable 3.5.1 — the hunt list tells you where the boss actually is

Ships **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.18**. Update both — the launcher writes the
mapping, the mod reads it.

## Only if you play with super-unique shuffle

That option swaps each named boss's monster base as a pair, which moves an
**identity** and never a spawn point. Treehead Woodfist keeps his name and his
hunt check — but he is now standing where some other named boss used to be, and
that boss is standing in someone else's spot.

None of the logic breaks. The permutation is a derangement over pairs, so every
hcIdx still exists exactly once and every hunt is still completable. Gate bosses
are never shuffled, so keys were never at risk, and neither are Radament, The
Summoner or Shenk, whose quests key on the monster itself.

What breaks is finding anything. The hunt list names a boss, and the boss is not
where the name says. "I can't find him, and when I cheat it, it spawns another
monster" — both are that, and both are what the option is supposed to do.

The hunt line now finishes with **"(at *someone*'s spot)"**, naming the boss
whose spawn point your target has taken over. You already know where the vanilla
bosses live, so that is enough to go on.

The launcher is the only thing that knows the permutation, because it builds it,
so it writes the mapping down and the mod reads it. With the shuffle off the
file is deleted rather than left behind: pointing somewhere wrong with total
confidence is worse than saying nothing.

**Not** fixed by this: The Summoner not counting for its hunt. That one is never
shuffled, so it is a different problem and still open.
Stable-3.5.1.title: Stable 3.5.1

Stable-3.5.2.description:
# Stable 3.5.2 — the hunt page says where

Ships **Multiworld Launcher 2.9.20**.

## Pitspawn Fouldog was in the wrong place

Not in the game — in our data. The logic had him in **Catacombs Level 1**. He has
always been in **Jail Level 2**, in a dead-end corner, which the game's own
presets say plainly: `Act1/Barracks/JailWPitspawn.ds1` and one each for E, S and
N. The name sends people to the Pit, the table sent the logic to the Catacombs,
and he was in neither.

Nothing was unreachable because of it — the hunt was gated on a *later* region
than the one it lives in, so the logic was merely pessimistic. But a key placed
at that check was held back further than it should have been, and three people
spent an evening looking in two wrong dungeons.

## Every hunt now prints its area

The quest page named a target and stopped there, which is fine until the name
lies. Select a hunt and it now reads **"Found in: Jail Level 2"** under the type.

The area comes from the same region map zone locking already gates on, so
nothing new is invented — whatever the logic believes, the book now says out
loud. That is the real value: a wrong entry becomes visible to players instead
of only to the generator. It is how the Pitspawn one was caught.

One trap worth recording: the mod's area-name table is zero-based over one-based
area ids, so entry *i* names area *i+1*. Indexed with a raw id it names the next
area along — which for a hunt would be exactly as unhelpful as saying nothing.
Checked against the game's own Levels.txt across twelve samples in two acts
before trusting it.
Stable-3.5.2.title: Stable 3.5.2

Stable-3.5.3.description:
# Stable 3.5.3

Tester-driven round. Everything here came from reports during the 4-player run.

## Checks could get stuck until you quit the game

A completed check sometimes sat there doing nothing, and only registered when the
player closed the game. In a multiworld that check may be another player's key, so
one idle player could stall someone else's run.

The deferred-quest queue was drained only from the window-message handler. That
sounds frequent, but it is driven by Windows messages: a player standing still in
fullscreen with no mouse or key input generates almost none. The queue is now also
drained from the render path, which runs every frame. It costs one variable read
when nothing is queued, so there is no performance trade.

The non-quest goal check (boss / uber / cow kills) hung on the same message pump and
now runs on a half-second timer for the same reason.

## The map forgot your exploration every time you saved and quit

The launcher deleted the whole map folder on every launch, to stop a new seed's
layout rendering on top of another seed's rooms. The folder is now stamped with the
seed it belongs to and only cleared when that stamp disagrees, so exploration
survives a save and quit and a new seed still starts clean.

## Whirlwind (and 47 other skills) showed the wrong mana cost

Whirlwind was listed at 25 mana where the real cost is 12.5, and the numbers stayed
double all the way up the level table.

`skills.txt` was correct. The book computed the cost from the raw columns and never
applied the `manashift` field, which scales them. That is harmless for the 118
skills whose shift is 8 (a multiplier of exactly 1), which is why this survived so
long -- but the other 48 all read too high, by 2x, 4x, 8x, and worse. Whirlwind's
shift of 7 is a halving. Half-point costs now print as "12.5" instead of rounding.

## Two monsters called Boneash

Gate guardians reuse the real boss's name, so the world contained two identically
named Boneash. Killing the guardian correctly does not credit the Hunt -- it has its
own spawn row precisely so the real target can still appear -- but nothing said so,
and the silence was indistinguishable from a broken check.

The 44 gate rows now carry their own names, and killing one while its Hunt is still
open says on screen that the Hunt wants the original.

## Act 2 and Act 3 Sewers checks are back

Sewers Level 1 and 2 had no clear check and no waypoint check while Level 3 did.
They were cut for "D2MOO pathfinding broken in narrow corridors" -- that root cause
was the bundled D2MOO D2Common, removed in 3.2.7, so the reason no longer holds.

Restored: Clear Sewers L1, Clear Sewers L2, Sewers Waypoint, Clear Kurast Sewers L1,
Clear Kurast Sewers L2 -- each with its zone mapping, so zone locking cannot place a
key behind its own gate.

## The book says where checks are

Quest pages now name the area for kill, waypoint and area checks -- 256 of them,
where a parsing bug had been silently limiting it to 102.

Hunts are deliberately excluded for now. Spot-checking Act 2 found Creeping Feature
listed in Palace Cellar when it is in Stony Tomb, plus Bloodwitch, Fangskin and Fire
Eye wrong as well. A line that confidently names the wrong room is worse than no line
at all. The hunt table will be rebuilt from the level presets and re-enabled once
every entry is checked.
Stable-3.5.3.title: Stable-3.5.3

Stable-3.5.4.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.5.4

## Gate keys can no longer strand you (zone locking)
The big one. With zone locking on, your Progressive Act Keys could be placed
anywhere in the multiworld — including behind another player's endgame. One
tester's second Act 1 key sat in someone else's Act 5, the third in their Act 5
*Nightmare*: nine zones to play, then nothing until that player finished the
game twice.

Generation now places every act's keys in the sphere of the act they open —
Act 1 keys in sphere 1, Act 2 in sphere 2, and so on through every difficulty.
Keys still travel into other players' games; they just can never sit deeper
than the act that needs them. The generator also self-verifies the chain and
refuses to produce a seed that breaks it.

**Regenerate your multiworld with the new apworld to get this protection.**
The launcher's Seed Check (updated in launcher 2.9.22) now audits any spoiler
for exactly this problem, so old seeds can be screened before you commit an
evening to them.

## The Summoner hunt completes
"Hunt: The Summoner" never fired: the engine places him directly from the
level preset, so kills bypassed the super-unique detection entirely. Kills of
preset-placed named bosses (The Summoner, Radament, Griswold, Nihlathak) are
now recognised by their unique monster class. Story credit was always fine —
this fixes the hunt check.

## Waypoint tracker told the wrong story
The HUD tracker had its own waypoint→area table, and its Act 2 tail was off by
one: standing in Far Oasis it looked up the Lost City waypoint and said
"[NOT FOUND]" forever, even after the check was sent and accepted. One table
now — the same one the detector uses.

## Quest-type toggles can no longer eat checks
Completing a quest while its type was toggled off stamped it "done" without
sending the check — permanently, even after re-enabling the type. The toggle
now refuses the completion instead of recording it, so the check fires when
you turn the type back on.

## Smaller fixes
- Gate-condition banner under AP now says "check sent — awaiting the key"
  instead of promising an unlock that hadn't arrived yet.
- Boss kills are always logged (the kill log used to stop after 50 lines,
  which made hunt reports impossible to diagnose).

Stable-3.5.5.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.5.5

## DeathLink actually kills you now
Receiving a DeathLink used to spawn a monster pack on your position — something
you could simply fight off, which made the whole pact meaningless. It now runs
the engine's own player-death routine: corpse, pets dismissed, respawn in town,
exactly as if a monster had landed the blow.

The first attempt used poison damage and did not work, for a reason worth
knowing: **in Diablo II poison can never kill a player** — it floors at 1 life
no matter how much you apply. The fix calls the death handler directly instead.

Two guards come with it:

- **A death caused by a DeathLink is never broadcast back.** Without that, two
  linked players kill each other in an endless loop.
- **Hardcore characters are exempt.** A DeathLink is not a good enough reason
  to end a hardcore run permanently; those players get the notification only.
  If the game cannot tell whether a character is hardcore, it refuses to kill.

Sending was already correct and is unchanged: only a real death is sent, never
a kick or a trap.

## Starting skills — a real setting, and always tier 1
How many skills you begin with is now an Archipelago option (`starting_skills`,
default 6), matching the setting standalone has always had. The game already
knew how to read it; the apworld simply never sent one.

Starting skills are now drawn from **tier 1 only** — the ten lowest-row skills
of each class — in Archipelago as well. Previously Archipelago handed out the
first few skills of a pool shuffled across all three tiers, so a run could open
on Frozen Orb or Blessed Hammer. Standalone never did this; the two modes now
agree.

## XP rewards up to 10,000,000
The XP reward minimum and maximum ceilings are raised from 1,000,000 to
10,000,000, in the game, the apworld and the launcher alike.

## Settings parity
Every Archipelago option now has a standalone counterpart and vice versa. The
gaps closed this round: the Collection gold target (Archipelago-only until now)
and the starting-skill count (standalone-only until now). The standalone skill
pool size slider is gone — the pool is the full set from the start, as
Archipelago has always done it.

Use launcher 2.9.23 or newer.
