Stable-3.5.6.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.5.6

A release about two things: three logic bugs that could quietly ruin a seed, and
the tracker finally telling you what is blocking you.

## Six of ten boss goals could never be completed

If your seed's goal was Pindleskin, Nihlathak, The Summoner, Radament, Izual or
the Council, **the goal could never fire and the seed could not be won.**

The kill detection matched on the wrong internal id. A wrong id here does not
mean "the wrong boss counts" — it means the number never arrives at all, so the
goal stays unfinished forever. Izual was worse: he is not a super-unique in the
first place, so he could never have matched any id. He now has his own detection
path. The Council is six separate super-uniques; all six now count.

This survived so long because the four ids that *were* correct all sit in the
range where the id column and the row number happen to be identical. The table
looked right at a glance.

## Rewards could land on the wrong player

With more than one player in the game, the code that looks up "which player is
this" took the first entry it found rather than yours. In single-player that is
the same thing; with two it was a coin toss for rewards, experience, gold,
stat and skill points, and the DeathLink kill. It now matches your own player.

## Act keys could be placed unreachably deep in other players' worlds

The important one, and it only shows up in large multiworlds.

Your Progressive Act Keys could be placed arbitrarily far into another player's
game — legal under Accessibility: Full, and completely unplayable: an Act 1 key
sitting in someone else's Act 5 Nightmare means you are stuck in Act 1 until
they get there. Keys are now placed so that an act's key is always available by
the time that act is.

Found and closed by generating seeds at 20, 30, 100, 200, 300 and 400 players,
twice each on different seed bases, plus a run with 300,000 locations. The
300-player round is the one that caught it.

⚠ **This changes seed generation. Existing seeds keep the old distribution — you
need to generate a new seed to get the fix.** Old seeds are not broken by it.

## The tracker now says what is blocking you

Two new lines, shown in town as well as in the field:

```
R3 LOCKED - Act2 Key2
  Kill: Radament
```

The second line has three different answers, and until now they all looked the
same from your side:

- `Chests 6/8` — in condition mode, your live progress toward the key
- `Kill: Radament` — the gate boss, under whatever name the shuffle gave him
- `sent - awaiting key` — **the check is already sent; there is nothing you can
  do but wait for the multiworld to hand you the key**

That last one is the reason the lines exist. "Go and do something" and "you are
waiting on someone else" were indistinguishable.

## The item feed names who sent it

Received items were logged as `(AP server)`, every one of them, while the
outgoing direction had always named the receiver correctly. The sender's name
was already travelling over the wire and had been for a long time — nothing ever
showed it to you. Now it does.

The DeathLink line said the name twice and credited the wrong one
(`DeathLink from Maegis (AP server)`); it now reads `DeathLink (Maegis)`.

## Launcher: where you are, and what you can reach

The Map tab has a status bar:

```
Sphere 7 of 15  —  Act 2 Nightmare  ·  2 of 4 gates open
Checks reachable now: 47 of 214 left
```

The sphere total follows your goal — a Full Normal run is 5 spheres, not 15.
The second line counts checks you have not done that are not behind a locked
door, so it answers the question you actually have: how much of what is left can
I go and do right now?

# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.5.7

## The launcher can complete a check in standalone

A new message from the launcher, `FORCECHECK`, lets the Map tab's **Cheat**
button work in a standalone game, where there is no Archipelago server to ask.

It runs the quest through the game's own completion path — the same one a real
clear goes through — so the reward is actually granted, the quest-type toggle is
honoured, and every counter moves. Setting the completed flag directly would
have marked the quest done and quietly skipped the reward, which is the opposite
of what the button promises.

It is deliberately not a general "set any flag" command: it names a quest and a
difficulty, and the game validates both before acting. A request for a
difficulty you are not currently playing is logged and ignored.

Nothing else changed in the mod. If you only play Archipelago, this release adds
nothing you will notice — the matching launcher update is the one that matters.

Stable-3.5.8.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.5.8

## Cheating in a Progressive Act Key now opens the gate you are stuck on

Giving yourself "Progressive Act 2 Key (Normal)" — from the launcher's item
dialog or with `!getitem` — always re-opened that act's **first** gate. If you
were stuck on gate 3, nothing happened, no matter how many times you tried.

The four copies of an act's key all share one item id; which gate a copy opens
is worked out from the check it came from. A key granted by cheat has no check
behind it, so it fell through to an old fallback meant for legacy bridges, and
that fallback always picked gate 1.

It now opens the next unopened gate instead. Reconnecting does not hand out
extra gates: the count is taken per session against what you already owned when
the first such key arrived, so the server replaying your item history re-grants
exactly the same gates rather than growing them.

Reported by fariel: *"Giving myself the item Progressive Act 2 Key (Normal)
didn't work. No combination of restarting, giving the item, etc worked."*

---

Both this and the matching launcher release (2.9.28) are worth taking. The
launcher one fixes a seed-generation bug that could make a seed unwinnable.

Stable-3.5.9.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.5.9

## The Treasure Cow actually pays out now

Two separate bugs, and they hid each other.

**It often dropped nothing at all.** The cow's death is spotted by polling its
unit pointer every tick. Diablo II recycles a corpse's unit from its pool, and
if that happened between two polls the code took a branch that logged "LOST —
no loot" and moved on. No drop, no message, nothing on screen. That is the only
path that produces exactly nothing with no trace, and it is almost certainly
what testers were hitting.

The game does not free a *live* monster in a loaded area, so a unit that
vanishes while you are still standing there is a dead one. That now counts as a
kill. Only leaving the area — a real unload — counts as a loss.

**And when it did work, the payout was ordinary.** The cow queued one boss loot
table: 3-5 items, exactly what any quest loot reward gives. It now queues
**twelve** — 36-60 items, dropped one table per 250 ms so they spread over about
three seconds instead of landing as a single heap.

The drain queue was also capped at 5, so raising the count alone would have
thrown two thirds of it away silently. The cap is 16 now.

You also get a notification and a line in `Archipelago/treasure_cow.log` on both
paths, so if a cow ever comes up short again the log says why instead of staying
quiet.

Reported by Maegis: *"Treasure cow dropped nothing."*
Stable-3.5.9.title: Stable 3.5.9

Stable-3.6.0.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.6.0

## The quest tracker can be locked in place

The tracker's drag handle sits over the play area, so a click that misses a
monster grabs it and drags the whole panel somewhere else. There is now a lock
button on the handle bar, just left of **Book**:

- `[ ]` — unlocked, the bar can be dragged as before
- `[L]` — locked in red, the bar ignores drags entirely

Click it to toggle. The grip dots disappear while locked, so the bar stops
inviting a drag it will refuse, and a short message confirms each change.

**Both the lock and the tracker's position are remembered between sessions.**
Place it once, lock it, and it stays there — a lock that forgot where you put it
would only solve half the problem. A stored position that no longer fits the
current resolution is ignored rather than parking the tracker off-screen where
its handle cannot be reached.

Unlock, move, lock again whenever you want to reposition it.

---

*Version note: this is 3.6.0 rather than 3.5.10 because the in-game version slot
holds 11 characters and "Stable3.5.10" needs 12. The build refuses to compile a
version that would not fit, which is why this is caught here rather than by
players seeing a corrupted string.*

Stable-3.6.1.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.6.1

## Skill points: vanilla level curve + a cap you control

Two new settings, both available in Archipelago YAMLs **and** in the launcher's
standalone settings. Both default to vanilla behaviour, and both can be turned
off completely.

### Skill Point Cap (new)

How many points may go into a single skill. **20 = vanilla.** Raise it up to 99
for the old "dump everything into one skill" behaviour.

Only invested points count — `+N to skill` bonuses from gear still stack on top
of the cap exactly as before.

### Skill Level Requirements (now escalates)

This toggle existed, but it only ever gated the *first* point: once you hit a
skill's required level, every remaining point could go in on that same level. A
level-30 character could drop forty points into an aura the moment it unlocked.

It now works the way the base game does — **the required level rises by 1 for
every point already invested**:

| Skill requires | 1st point | 5th point | 10th point | 20th point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| level 1  | level 1  | level 5  | level 10 | level 20 |
| level 6  | level 6  | level 10 | level 15 | level 25 |
| level 12 | level 12 | level 16 | level 21 | level 31 |
| level 18 | level 18 | level 22 | level 27 | level 37 |
| level 24 | level 24 | level 28 | level 33 | level 43 |
| level 30 | level 30 | level 34 | level 39 | level 49 |

So a level-30 skill needs character level 49 before it can hold 20 points. The
power curve stays smooth without capping how strong a build can eventually get.

Turn the toggle **off** and there is no level gate at all — any unlocked skill
takes points at any level, up to the cap. Combined with a cap of 99 that
reproduces the old free-for-all exactly.

**Existing characters are safe.** A character that already holds more points in
a skill than the new cap keeps every one of them; it simply cannot add more.

Both settings are frozen per character at creation, like every other setting, so
switching profiles never rewrites a character you are part-way through.

---

Thanks to Yllarius for the detailed balance write-up that prompted this, and to
Maegis for triaging it.
Stable-3.6.1.title: Stable-3.6.1

Stable-3.6.2.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.6.2

## XP and gold rewards now scale with your level

An XP reward used to be a random number picked from a slider — the same roll
whether you found it in the Blood Moor or in Hell. That is why fariel could open
a chest in Cold Plains, take a ten-million-XP filler, hit level 30, equip Holy
Shock and walk to Act 3 without fighting a single monster.

Raising the ceiling could never have fixed it either. The slider stopped at
10,000,000, while level 60 → 61 alone costs **11,009,646** — the very same number
that trivialises Act 1 is a rounding error in Hell.

**An XP reward is now worth exactly one level, whatever level you are.**

The amount comes from the game's own experience table, so it is vanilla by
construction:

| Your level | XP reward | Gold reward |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 500 | 100 |
| 10 | 14,429 | 10,000 |
| 30 | 829,810 | 90,000 |
| 50 | 4,650,593 | 250,000 |
| 70 | 26,063,836 | 490,000 |
| 90 | 146,072,446 | 810,000 |
| 99 | — (at the cap) | 980,100 |

Any leftover experience carries into the next level exactly as it always has, so
nothing is wasted. At level 99 an XP reward pays out as gold instead of vanishing.

**Gold works the same way** — it scales with your level instead of rolling a flat
1–10,000, which stopped being worth bending down for somewhere in Act 2.

This applies everywhere a reward can come from: Archipelago items, quest
rewards, shrines, urns, barrels, chests, and every extra check.

### Settings removed

The four reward-amount sliders — **Gold reward minimum/maximum** and **XP reward
minimum/maximum** — are gone from both the YAML options and the launcher's
standalone settings. There is no longer an amount to configure; the level decides
it. Existing YAMLs and standalone profiles that still list them keep working, the
values are simply ignored.

The **XP bonus** multiplier for monster kills is untouched.

---

Thanks to fariel for the write-up that pinned this down, and to Maegis and
Yllarius for working through it.
Stable-3.6.2.title: Stable-3.6.2

Stable-3.6.3.description:
# Diablo II Archipelago — Stable 3.6.3

## The Treasure Cow now drops chests

Killing the Treasure Cow spawns **3 to 5 sparkling chests** in a ring around
you. Open them at your own pace.

### Why it changed

The cow used to pay out through the mod's own item-delivery path — build the
items, hand them to the player. That path is where every "the cow dropped
nothing" report came from: it has to get item quality, inventory space and
delivery flags right every single time, and when any one of those went wrong the
reward silently vanished.

So the mod stops making items altogether. It spawns real chests and lets Diablo
II do what it has always done well.

### Why these chests are worth opening

They are the sparkling kind — the same ones you hunt for in the wild. The game's
own chest code treats them specially:

- every item rolls at **magic** quality, and 5% of the time **rare**
- they skip the 25% "drops nothing" gate an ordinary chest has to pass
- if nothing magic came out, the game **rerolls up to ten more times** until
  something does

A sparkling chest cannot come up empty. That is a guarantee from the game
itself, not from us — which is exactly the point.

### If something goes wrong

The mod checks that it recognises your game build before spawning anything. On
an unexpected build it quietly falls back to the old item reward instead, so a
killed cow is never unrewarded. The reason is written to the log either way.

Both the confirmed kill and the "cow vanished while you were still standing
there" case pay out the same way.

# Diablo II Archipelago — Unstable 3.6.4

## The channel is now called Unstable

It used to say "Stable". That promised more than it should: this is a project
that ships fixes the same day they are found, and several releases in a day is
normal. "Unstable" is the honest label.

Nothing about how it works has changed. In game the version reads `U-3.6.4` —
the slot Diablo II gives us holds eleven characters, and the full word does not
fit next to a version number.

## The Treasure Cow is a real super-unique now

**Every cow in the Cow Level was called "Archipelago Treasure Cow".** That was
not a display bug — the Treasure Cow was an ordinary Hell Bovine, and the only
way to give it a name was to rename the monster *type* in the string table.
That renames every Hell Bovine in the game, all thousands of them.

So the Treasure Cow got its own entry in the super-unique table, and the Hell
Bovine has its vanilla name back. **The Cow Level reads normally again.**

The cow still comes alone, still hits like a boss, and it can appear more than
once in a session.

## Killing it drops chests

The cow used to pay out by handing items straight to you, which is where every
"the cow dropped nothing" report came from. It now spawns **3 to 5 sparkling
chests** around you instead, and Diablo II's own chest code does the rest:

- every item rolls at magic quality, 5% of the time rare
- they skip the 25% "drops nothing" gate an ordinary chest has to pass
- if nothing magic came out, the game rerolls up to ten more times

A sparkling chest cannot come up empty. That guarantee is the game's, not ours.

If the mod does not recognise your game build it quietly falls back to the old
item reward rather than spawning nothing, and says so in the log.

## Testing it

The cheat menu (Ctrl+V) has a **Treasure Cow** button under Mons → Bosses, so
you can spawn one where you stand instead of waiting for it to turn up.

## Source code

The full source is now on GitHub alongside the release, for both this line and
the experimental one.

# Diablo II Archipelago — Unstable 3.6.5

## The cheat menu fits the screen now

Some tabs — Runes, Gems and Misc under Loot — were taller than the screen at
800x600. The panel centred itself on its own height, so on those tabs the title
bar with the close button sat up to 67 pixels above the top edge and the last
rows below the bottom one, with no way to reach either.

The panel now caps its height to the screen and the content scrolls instead:
mouse wheel over the panel, scrollbar on the right edge, and each tab remembers
its own position. Tabs that fit are unchanged.

## Choose how many skills are in the pool

New option in both the Archipelago YAML (**Skill Pool Size**) and the
launcher's standalone settings (a checkbox plus a slider). Off, or 0, means
what it has always meant: every skill that passes the class filter.

Set it to 30 and the pool is exactly 30 skills — **10 tier-1, 10 tier-2 and
10 tier-3, picked at random**. The split stays even at any value, the class
filter is applied first, and the skill locations that no longer hold a skill
fill with ordinary filler instead.

## Tested

This release went through the full logic battery: every option at both
extremes, the risky combinations (gates x entrances x goals, now including the
new pool cap against all of them), 300 randomised option sets, a mixed
multiworld, all 56 custom goals, a 126-slot world with ~300,000 foreign
locations, and the gate-key placement audit — 360 key placements, none
unreachable. The sweep also caught two real bugs in this feature before
release, which is exactly what it is for.

## Launcher 2.9.35

- **Volume slider** for the notification sounds, defaulting to 50%.
- **Add your own sound** — pick a wav, mp3 or wma and it appears in the
  per-event sound lists. Your files live in their own folder that updates
  never touch.

Unstable-3.6.6.description:
# Unstable 3.6.6

Rewards you can plan around. 33 new filler items, and where they land now
depends on how far into the run you are.

## Tiered rewards land at a matching depth

High runes, perfect gems, grand charms and the big point items are held back
for the later acts and difficulties. Their low-tier counterparts come early.
A Vex is no longer exactly as likely in Blood Moor as in Hell Act 5.

Measured over a full seed: **100% of tiered rewards now land inside their
band, against 62-66% before.**

The bands scale to the seed. A Full Normal run only spans Act 1 through Act 5
Normal, so the whole ladder is squeezed onto that — the order survives even
when "late" means Act 4 Normal instead of Act 3 Hell.

New option **Tiered Filler Depth** (on by default) in both the AP YAML and the
standalone settings. Turn it off for the old flat roll. It only moves filler,
so logic and reachability are identical either way.

## New rewards

**Tiered bundles** — Random Rune (Mid), Random Rune (High), Flawless Gem,
Perfect Gem, Small Charm, Large Charm, Grand Charm. The high rune band runs
Pul through Ohm; Lo and above stay out of the filler pool.

**Point items in real sizes** — 1, 3 and 10 Stat Points; 1, 2 and 3 Skill
Points; 1 and 3 Reset Points. Named honestly, so what the multiworld shows
other players is what you actually receive.

**Gear by slot** — set and unique drops split into armour, helm, shield,
gloves, boots, belt, weapon and jewelry. "Drop: Unique Boots" now means boots.

## New traps

- **Barrel Field** — a ring of exploding barrels around you
- **Urn Garden** — a floor of urns to wade through
- **False Treasure** — six chests, two of which are not chests
- **Junk Backpack** — twenty useless items into your pack

The first three hold until you leave town. All four also appear in standalone
runs.

## Fixes

- **Standalone was missing twelve reward types.** The ordinary-item bundles
  added in 3.6.5 were only ever wired into the Archipelago roll — a standalone
  character could never receive them. All 19 bundles and all 8 trap types now
  roll in both modes.
- The Treasure Cow's chests and the new object traps now share one spawner
  instead of two copies of the same code.

## Verified

Generation checked across the smoke, isolate, risky and multiworld option
sweeps in both lines. A 300-player multiworld generated clean: 522 gate keys
placed, zero depth violations.
Unstable-3.6.6.title: Unstable 3.6.6

Unstable-3.6.7.description:
# Unstable 3.6.7

A loot filter. Choose what colour each kind of drop is drawn in, or stop
drawing it at all.

## Where

**Launcher → Settings → Diablo II → Loot Filter → "Colours and hiding…"**

Twenty-two groups, each with a colour and a Hide box:

**By type** — gold, runes, gems, charms, jewels, rings and amulets, health and
mana potions, rejuvenation, throwing potions, antidote/thawing/stamina,
scrolls, tomes, keys, arrows and bolts, quest items.

**By quality** — normal, superior, magic, rare, set, unique, crafted.

Ten colours: white, red, green, blue, gold, grey, tan, orange, yellow, or
Default to leave it exactly as the game draws it.

Everything starts at Default, so if you never open the dialog nothing about
your game changes. The setting is remembered across seeds and applies to both
Archipelago and standalone runs.

Gold as orange, runes in their own colour, plain white gear gone entirely —
whatever you want.

## Read this before you turn it on

**This is the first release of the filter and it is not fully proven.**

Diablo II does not keep item colours in any data file; it decides them in
code. The only way to change them is to intercept the game's drawing calls,
and that interception sees *every* piece of text the game client draws — menus
and shop lists included, not just labels on the ground.

There is a guard: a rule only applies to text that arrived with a backdrop
behind it, which ground labels have and menu text does not. It should be
enough. It has not been confirmed in a real session.

So: if you set a rule and text goes missing somewhere it should not, that is
this. Open the dialog and press **Reset all to default** — it takes effect on
the next launch, no reinstall and no waiting for a patch.

There is a **"Log every item label"** box at the bottom of the dialog. Turning
it on for a minute and sending the resulting `d2arch_log.txt` is what will
settle whether the guard holds.

## Also

The mod's import-patching helper now handles ordinal imports, which is how the
Diablo II modules export nearly everything. That is what made the filter
reachable at all.

Unstable-3.6.8.description:
# Unstable 3.6.8

## The loot filter is gone again

3.6.7 added a filter for recolouring and hiding item labels on the ground. It
did not work, and it is removed.

The honest version of what happened: Diablo II decides those colours in code
rather than in any data file, so changing them means intercepting the game's
drawing calls. Which call to intercept could not be established from the
binary — the function that reads the Alt key, which is the one that decides
whether to label items at all, makes no drawing call anywhere near itself. The
release went out on a reasonable guess with a fallback plan, and the fallback
is this patch.

Nothing else in 3.6.7 was affected, and nothing carried over: the mod no longer
contains the code, and the launcher writes the filter off on every launch so a
mismatched pair of versions cannot leave it running.

Everything from 3.6.6 — tiered reward depth, the 33 new filler items, the four
object traps — is untouched.

Unstable-3.6.9.description:
# Unstable 3.6.9

Debug menu (Ctrl+V), Character tab.

## Two new buttons

**+100M XP** — exactly one hundred million experience. From a fresh character
that lands you at level 57.

**Max Level** — straight to 99. There because 100M is not actually enough to
reach the Pandemonium content: from level 90 it does not even give you one
more level.

Both stop at 99 rather than doing anything, and say so in the log.

## +10 Levels now gives ten levels

It used to hand over a flat 500,000 experience regardless of where you were.
That is roughly thirty levels at level 1 and next to nothing at level 80 — the
button had been lying about what it did.

It now reads your level and adds the actual gap to level+10.

## Under the hood

Level 99 costs 3,837,739,017 experience, which does not fit in the signed
32-bit value the game's stat call takes. A large grant is handed over in
pieces, and never more than the room left below the cap — adding past it wraps
the total negative, and the character would look like it had lost every level
it had.

Launcher unchanged at 2.9.38.

# Diablo II Archipelago

A randomizer mod for Diablo II: Lord of Destruction (1.10f) with [Archipelago](https://archipelago.gg/) multiworld support.

Randomizes skill unlocks across a quest system spanning all 5 Acts. Complete quests to earn skills from any of the 7 character classes. Play solo with custom settings or connect to an Archipelago multiworld server for cross-game randomization.

---

## Features

- **210 Skills** from all 7 classes (Amazon, Sorceress, Necromancer, Paladin, Barbarian, Druid, Assassin) randomized into a quest reward pool
- **231 Quests** across 5 Acts: Story, Super Unique Hunting, Zone Clears, Exploration, Waypoints, Level Milestones
- **Skill Editor** (F1): Assign unlocked skills to your build with 3 tabs and 10 slots per tab
- **Quest Log** (F2): Track progress with Main/Side quest tabs, scrollbar, and per-difficulty tracking
- **Quest Tracker HUD** (F3): Shows current objectives and goal progress
- **Trap System**: Certain quests spawn dangerous Super Unique monsters near you
- **Reset Points**: Earned from quests, used to reassign skills
- **Tier System**: T1 (Level 1+), T2 (Level 20+), T3 (Level 40+) skill gating
- **Archipelago Integration**: Full multiworld support with item sending/receiving, DeathLink, and goal tracking
- **Configurable Settings**: Quest types, skill pool size, filler distribution, and more

---

## Installation

### Requirements
- Diablo II + Lord of Destruction (original installation required)
- Windows 10 or later

### Steps
1. Download the latest release ZIP from [Releases](https://github.com/solida1987/Diablo-II-Archipelago/releases)
2. Extract the ZIP anywhere on your computer
3. Run **D2ArchSetup.exe**
4. Click Browse and select your Diablo II installation folder
5. Click Install
6. Launch with **Play Archipelago.exe**

The installer copies required files from your Diablo II installation. Your original game is not modified.

---

## How to Play

### Singleplayer
1. Run **Play Archipelago.exe**
2. Select **Singleplayer**
3. Configure game settings (goal scope, quest types, skill pool, filler distribution)
4. Click **Play**
5. Create a new character or continue an existing one

### Archipelago Multiworld
1. Install the **.apworld** file (found in files/Archipelago/) into your Archipelago installation
2. Generate a multiworld with your YAML settings
3. Host or connect to an AP server
4. Run **Play Archipelago.exe**
5. Select **Archipelago**
6. Enter server address, slot name, and password
7. Click **Play**

The console window shows AP connection status and events in real-time.

---

## Controls

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| F1 | Open/Close Skill Editor |
| F2 | Open/Close Quest Log |
| F3 | Toggle Quest Tracker HUD |
| ESC | Close any open panel |

---

## AP World Options (YAML)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| goal_scope | Choice | full_game | Act 1 only / Acts 1-2 / Acts 1-3 / Acts 1-4 / Full Game |
| difficulty_scope | Choice | normal_only | Normal / Normal+Nightmare / All Three |
| quest_story | Toggle | true | Include story quests |
| quest_hunting | Toggle | true | Include Super Unique hunting quests |
| quest_kill_zones | Toggle | true | Include zone clear quests |
| quest_exploration | Toggle | true | Include area entry quests |
| quest_waypoints | Toggle | true | Include waypoint quests |
| quest_level_milestones | Toggle | true | Include level milestone quests |
| skill_pool_size | 20-210 | 210 | Number of skills in the item pool |
| starting_skills | 1-20 | 6 | Skills unlocked at start |
| filler_gold_pct | 0-100 | 30 | Gold filler weight |
| filler_stat_pts_pct | 0-100 | 15 | Stat point filler weight |
| filler_skill_pts_pct | 0-100 | 15 | Skill point filler weight |
| filler_trap_pct | 0-100 | 15 | Trap filler weight |
| filler_reset_pts_pct | 0-100 | 25 | Reset point filler weight |
| starting_gold | 0-50000 | 0 | Starting gold amount |
| death_link | Toggle | false | Enable DeathLink |

---

## Built With

- [D2MOO](https://github.com/nicodoctor/D2MOO) - Diablo II open-source reimplementation for D2Common, D2Game, and Fog DLLs
- [D2.Detours](https://github.com/nicodoctor/D2.Detours) - DLL patching and injection framework
- [cnc-ddraw](https://github.com/FunkyFr3sh/cnc-ddraw) - Graphics wrapper for windowed mode on modern Windows
- [Archipelago](https://archipelago.gg/) - Cross-game multiworld randomizer framework

## Credits

- **solida** - Project lead, game systems, quest design, AP integration
- **D2MOO Team** - Open-source Diablo II reimplementation
- **Archipelago Community** - Multiworld framework and support
- **Diablo II Modding Community** - Research, tools, and documentation

## License

This project is a modification for Diablo II: Lord of Destruction. A legal copy of the original game is required to play.

## Diablo II Archipelago beta-1.5.1

Bugfix release based on full codebase audit. 12 bugs fixed.

### Critical Fixes
- **AP Bridge**: Fixed WebSocket dependency missing in packaged build (No module named websockets.asyncio)
- **Save Path**: Fixed save directory detection failing silently - now has 4-level fallback chain with logging
- **SuperUnique Hunts**: Fixed Corpsefire and other hunt kills not registering - added UNITFLAG_ISDEAD check
- **AP Reconnect**: Fixed filler items (gold, stat points, traps) duplicating on reconnect
- **Quest ID Collision**: Fixed duplicate quest ID 57 (Hole Level 1 vs Catacombs Waypoint) - 4 missing locations added

### Gameplay Fixes
- **Singleplayer Sync**: Gold, stat points, and skill points now show immediately instead of requiring save-exit
- **XP Multiplier**: Fixed counterproductive ExpRatio modification - now correctly divides level thresholds only
- **Assassin Weapons**: Katars (h2h) removed from shops to prevent crash when equipped by non-Assassin classes
- **Skill Points**: Fixed skill points jumping to wrong skills after reload - reinvest now validates against current tree
- **Boss Shuffle**: Improved randomization - retry mechanism ensures 75%+ of bosses actually change position

### Technical
- Dead monster tracking: circular buffer instead of full reset on overflow
- AP items_received_index: persistent to disk, prevents item loss on bridge restart
- Forward declaration fix for Log() function (compile error prevention)
- Full codebase audit documentation in Research/FULL_CODEBASE_MAP.md

v3.7.0.description:
# v3.7.0

## The version is just a number now

No more Beta, Stable or Unstable. Each of those made a promise about the build
that the number already says better, and the last rename was itself a reaction
to "Stable" claiming too much. A bare version claims nothing.

`Unstable-3.6.9` was the last of the old spelling; this is `v3.7.0`.

## Hunts now say where the target actually is

With the super-unique shuffle on, a hunt's target keeps its name but stands on
some other boss's spawn point. Three separate displays were supposed to tell
you that. None of them did, for three different reasons:

**The quest book showed nothing at all.** The code that looks up the moved
target's real location sat behind a condition that could never be true — the
line above it had already ruled out every hunt. It was dead from the day it was
written.

**Zone names were off by one.** The area name table is indexed by area id
directly, but the book read it one slot low, so every zone on the page named
its neighbour. This is very likely why the hunt areas were written off as
untrustworthy at the time: the table was right, the reading was wrong.

**The in-game tracker named the host but not the place.** It now says both.

A hunt reads `Found in: Black Marsh (at Rakanishu's spot)` when shuffled, and
its own verified zone when not.

## Boss loot was invisible in solo runs

Every reward type announces itself so the launcher can log it and play a sound.
Boss loot said "Awesome loot incoming!", which carried none of the markers the
solo pipe filters on — so it produced no tracker entry and no sound, and always
had. It now announces itself like everything else:
`Drop: Andariel Loot (4 items)`.

Traps had the same problem and are fixed alongside.

## Debug menu

Unchanged from 3.6.9: `+100M XP`, `Max Level`, and `+10 Levels` giving ten
actual levels.

Requires launcher 2.9.39.

v3.7.1.description:
# v3.7.1 — Crash & stability round (safe mid-run)

Every fix in this release is runtime-only: nothing changes the generated world,
the check list, or item placement. It is safe to update in the middle of an
ongoing multiworld — that is the whole point of it.

## Crash fixes

- **Fixed the "cow crash"** (assertion in UnitRoom.cpp / DungeonTestRoomGame).
  Every spawn the mod performs — Treasure Cow, cow hoard chests, trap ambushes,
  object traps — now resolves the room that actually CONTAINS the target
  coordinates before spawning. Previously the player's own room was passed with
  far-away coordinates, and the game asserts on that mismatch instead of
  failing gracefully; the cow's "30 placement attempts" never got a second try.
  The cow also spawns closer now (25-100 yards instead of 40-300), so its
  placement lands inside loaded terrain.
- **Fixed the texture-cache crash** (glTextureCache.cpp / tTempItem). Object
  traps (barrels / urns / false treasure) only spawn object types that are
  already present in the area around you — an act-foreign object has no loaded
  graphics and killed the renderer. A trap that cannot fire safely fizzles
  silently instead of crashing.

## Traps

- **A "Trap: Monsters" filler no longer announces itself as the Monster Revive
  Trap.** The ambush queue now remembers who queued it: reward traps say
  "TRAP! Monsters incoming!", only the actual Revive Trap says "The slain rise
  against you!". (The Revive Trap toggle itself always worked — the message
  was lying.)

## Item delivery / progression

- **Raised both redelivery-protection caps** (applied-item ids 4096 → 16384,
  filler locations 2048 → 8192) and made hitting a cap log loudly. Anything
  that fell off these lists silently was re-delivered on the next reconnect —
  the "save & quit gave me 28 skill points" report.
- **Settings now survive save & load correctly:** `xp_multiplier` was clamped
  by a leftover 1-10 guard on load (the setting goes 0-100 — an x25 player
  lost the multiplier every restart), and `skill_max_level` +
  `skill_level_reqs` were written to the state file but never read back.

## Gameplay

- **Treasure Cow rebalanced:** max 3 per act (was 5), 8% chance per area
  (was 25%), and early-act HP bonuses roughly halved. A boss-tier cow in Den
  of Evil at level 1 was not a fair fight. `treasure_cows.dat` overrides still
  apply if present.
- **After a crash you can no longer keep a skill you don't own on left/right
  click** — the mod now validates hand-assigned skills continuously and resets
  unowned ones to Attack.
- **One kill can no longer complete two Hunts.** A super-unique's minions
  share the boss's class, and the class-match fallback credited the minions'
  hunt on top of the boss's own — minions and champions are now excluded from
  fallback crediting.
- **Clear Monastery Gate / Clear Inner Cloister** are now reach-the-area
  checks. Those zones spawn almost no monsters, so "kill 8" meant dragging
  monsters in from next door. Same treatment as the Tower Cellar fix in 3.0.0.

## Entrance shuffle

- **Exiting a cross-act shuffled dungeon returns you to the entrance you came
  from** instead of bouncing you town-to-town. The act-town lock used to wipe
  the recorded way home (this is what broke the Cain quest for one player),
  and zone-locking could override the return warp in the same tick. The
  original entrance always wins now.

## UI

- **The HUD tracker no longer draws on top of the open Book.**
